job.title: Service Scheduler & Administration Coordinator

What you’ll bring
  • At least 2 years of scheduling experience in Simpro, AroFlo or similar job management software. 5+ years is highly regarded.

What’s in it for you
  • Immediate start, with a full handover

  • The potential to go permanent for the right person
Apply now

job.title: Senior Town Planner
job.description:
Senior Town Planner

Our Client de Witt Consulting is a well-established and respected Surveying, Town Planning, Ecology and Project Management company. We are seeking a Senior Town Planner to join their team.

Their Town Planning section undertakes large and small projects across residential, commercial, education, rural, renewable energy, industrial and infrastructure sectors.  Projects span NSW thanks to offices in the Lower Hunter, Mid-Western, Mid-Coast and Central Coast regions of NSW.  They guide, advise and support our clients through all project stages from concept, approval through to construction.  

Based in the Newcastle office, the successful applicant would benefit from an attractive employment package with the option for flexible working conditions.  de Witt Consulting offers pathways for career progression, the opportunity to work on a diverse range of projects as part of a multidisciplinary team of town planners, surveyors, ecologists and project managers, professional membership to PIA and opportunities to attend networking events and industry functions.

The Town Planning team is supportive and passionate about our work and clients and thrives on attention to detail and a positive attitude to match!  Be challenged and excited by the opportunities this role has to offer! 

The successful applicant would ideally have all of the following skills, experiences and qualifications:
  • Qualification in Urban and Regional Planning or related discipline.
  • At least 5 years’ experience in the Town Planning profession, preferably within the NSW planning system.
  • Customer and quality focus.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Current NSW Driver's Licence.
This is a senior technical role offering flexibility, autonomy, and long-term career progression—without immediate Principal-level pressure.

Please apply online or call 0437 356 484 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Lead the Future of the Harvey Region

Situated between Perth and Bunbury, the Shire of Harvey is home to more than 32,000 residents and combines a thriving economy with an enviable Southwest lifestyle. With strong population growth, diverse industries and communities, significant development opportunities and a highly engaged community, the Shire offers a rare opportunity for an exceptional leader to shape the future of a region defined by growth, opportunity and quality of life.

The Shire of Harvey offers more than a leadership role. It provides the opportunity to lead within an organisation that values integrity, collaboration and continuous improvement. Supported by a strong organisational culture, professional development opportunities, employee wellbeing initiatives and a commitment to work-life balance, the Shire is focused on attracting and retaining high-performing leaders who are passionate about delivering lasting outcomes for their communities.

Joining the Shire of Harvey is more than a career opportunity. It is an opportunity to become part of a vibrant and welcoming community that values connection, contribution and shared success. The region's strong community spirit, rich natural environment and commitment to growth create a rewarding setting for leaders who are motivated by purpose, enjoy building relationships and are passionate about creating positive outcomes for the people and places they serve. The ideal candidate will embrace the opportunity to become an active and visible member of the community, sharing a genuine passion for the region, its people and its future, and fostering strong connections that help shape lasting outcomes.

Link https://harveyregion.com.au/
 

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to Council, the Chief Executive Officer will provide strategic leadership, organisational stewardship and operational management of the Shire. The CEO will lead the implementation of Council's vision and priorities while ensuring the delivery of sustainable community outcomes, major infrastructure projects, responsible financial management and exemplary governance practices.
Key priorities include:
  • Leading the delivery of Council's Council Plan 2025 – 2035
  • Driving major infrastructure, planning and development initiatives that support growth and economic prosperity.
  • Building a high-performing and customer-focused organisational culture.
  • Ensuring robust governance, accountability and legislative compliance.
  • Develop and strengthen relationships with Councillors, community members, government agencies and industry stakeholders.
  • Maintain and improve the Shire's long-term financial sustainability and organisational performance.
 
About You

We are seeking an accomplished Chief Executive Officer with a demonstrated ability to lead complex organisations and deliver strategic outcomes.
You will bring:
  • Proven experience as a Chief Executive Officer within local government, the public sector or another complex service-based organisation.
  • Strong governance and political acumen, with experience working effectively with Boards, Councils and governing bodies.
  • Experience leading major infrastructure, planning, development or growth initiatives.
  • Outstanding stakeholder engagement and relationship management capability.
  • Strong commercial and financial leadership skills.
  • A genuine commitment to community outcomes, organisational culture and public value.
 
Why Harvey?

This is a unique opportunity to lead one of the fastest growing regional local governments in Western Australia at a time of significant opportunity and transformation. With an engaged Council, ambitious strategic agenda, major infrastructure opportunities and an exceptional quality of life, the Shire of Harvey offers a rewarding leadership role where you can make a genuine and lasting impact.

Set between the coast and countryside, the Shire offers an enviable lifestyle supported by excellent community infrastructure, including 16 schools, four libraries, recreation and aquatic centres, comprehensive health services, diverse housing options and convenient retail amenities. Residents enjoy 42 kilometres of coastline, extensive parks and open spaces, a vibrant calendar of community events, a wide range of sporting and community clubs, and an outstanding selection of cafés, restaurants and local produce, making Harvey an ideal place to live, work and raise a family.
 
 
Salary Package

A negotiable remuneration package, aligned with Local Government Band 2 requirements, will be offered to the successful candidate.
 
Application Process

Closing date: 17th November 2026

To submit your application, please provide a current resume and a cover letter of no more than two pages outlining your suitability for the role.

Applications can be made by clicking apply.

A candidate information pack is available here:

https://irp.cdn-website.com/0ba2c165/files/uploaded/Candidate+Pack_UPDATED.pdf

Enquiries: For a confidential discussion on the role, you may contact Craig Moffat at Chandler Macleod on 0447 571 643.
job.salary: Negotiable, aligned with Local Government Band 2

job.title: Onsite Consultant (Multiple positions: Day, night & sunrise shifts)
job.description:
About the roles
We are currently recruiting for multiple Onsite Consultant opportunities across two large, high-volume distribution centres located in Kemps Creek and Horsley Park.
 
These are hands-on, people-focused roles where you will be responsible for supporting and managing a large casual workforce. Acting as the primary point of contact for employees on site, you will oversee day-to-day workforce requirements, monitor attendance and performance, address employee concerns and ensure workplace standards are maintained.
 
Working closely with operational stakeholders, you will play an important role in maintaining workforce engagement, ensuring adequate staffing coverage and supporting the smooth day-to-day operation of the distribution centre.
There are multiple permanent opportunities available across different shift patterns, including:
 
  • Day Shift: Full-time opportunities, 7am to  6pm on a 7 day rotating roster (Week 1 Wednesday – Saturday. Week 2 Thursday – Saturday)
  • Night Shift: Full-time opportunities, 5:30pm to 4:30am on a 7 day rotating roster (Week 1 Wednesday – Saturday. Week 2 Thursday – Saturday)
  • Sunrise Consultant: Part-time, 3:30am – 8:30am (Week 1 Wednesday – Saturday. Week 2 Thursday – Saturday)
 
When applying, please indicate your preferred shift arrangement – day shift, night shift or part-time early mornings (Sunrise Consultant).
 
Duties
  • Act as the primary point of contact for a large casual workforce
  • Monitor daily attendance, absenteeism, punctuality and workforce coverage
  • Manage employee performance, conduct and behavioural concerns, escalating issues where required
  • Monitor workplace presentation, hygiene and compliance with site standards
  • Build strong working relationships with employees, providing ongoing support and guidance
  • Manage employee queries, concerns and day-to-day workplace issues
  • Liaise with operational stakeholders regarding workforce requirements, performance and productivity
  • Maintain accurate employee records, reporting and workforce documentation
  • Assist with employee onboarding, inductions and general administration
 
Skills and Experience
  • Experience in a people-focused, fast-paced environment, such as team leadership, customer service, hospitality, retail, recruitment or workforce coordination
  • Previous experience supervising, supporting or coordinating a team, with the ability to manage competing demands
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport across all levels
  • Confidence managing challenging conversations and addressing performance or attendance issues
  • Highly organised with strong administration and time management skills
  • Resilient and adaptable, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive, hands-on approach
 
Benefits
  • Permanent employment opportunities
  • Full-time and part-time positions available
  • Multiple locations and shift options
  • Structured rotating rosters with regular days off
 
How to apply
Sound interesting? We would love to hear from you! Click APPLY NOW to upload a copy of your current resume, or call 02 6691 9100.
 
Please specify your preferred shift arrangement in your application: Day Shift, Night Shift or Part-Time Early Mornings (3:30am–8:30am).

job.title: Pick Packer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod has an exciting opportunity available, to working for one of Australia’s leading Supply chains located in Dandenong VIC. 
 
We are recruiting Pick Packers to work within a Warehouse facility to unwrap pallets, sort stock and manual Voice picking requirements. Applicants with a Forklift licence and experience are encouraged to apply. 
 
These opportunities are for hours across  Afternoon 2pm – 10pm and Night 10pm – 6am Shifts and have the view to Permanent Part Time Roles! 
 
If you are looking for an exciting opportunity to join the leader in logistics and technology, then please read on … 
 
Duties and Responsibilities: 
 
Reporting to the Manual Pick Area Specialist you will be required to perform a variety of duties that will be offered on a rotation basis, duties include but not limited to: 
 
•             Removing wrapping and sorting boxes from pallets 
•             Haul pallets on a transporter following the site traffic management plan to the drop off point. 
•             Receipting pallets from vendors and Primary Freight, as well as reporting noncompliance and rejections. 
•             Required to scan the pallets SSCC label and take the pallet to the location indicated on the screen. 
•             Forklift operation – Replenishing products using state of the art technology. 
•             Voice picking required to pick orders onto pallets and shrink wrap products to holding point. 
To be successful for this role you must be able to: 
 
•             Be flexible for 5 shifts per week across Monday to Sunday (weekend work as required) 
•             Available for Day, Afternoon shifts or Night Shifts – It’s advantageous if you are available for any shift 
•             Be an experienced Forklift operator with proven work experience (*Forklift Roles only) 
•             Voice Picking experience (highly advantageous) 
•             Transporter / Tugger experience (highly advantageous) 
•             Strong team player who can work in a dynamic and diverse work environment 
•             Excellent attention to detail 
•             Reliable, punctual and trustworthy 
•             You will be required to participate in a pre-employment medical prior to commencement which will include drug/alcohol testing. 
 
Don’t miss out on the fantastic opportunity. Click on the “Apply Now” prompt below to submit your resume today.

job.title: Families and Programs Visitor Engagement Officers
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is partnering with the Australian National Maritime Museum to find energetic, creative and people-focused Families & Programs Visitor Engagement Officers to join the team in Pyrmont, NSW. 

These casual roles offer varied shifts over an initial three-month engagement, with the possibility of extension. More importantly, they are an opportunity to work at one of Sydney’s most iconic cultural institutions, where no two days are quite the same and you can make a genuine difference to a visitor’s experience. 

ABOUT THE MUSEUM 

The Australian National Maritime Museum is one of the world’s leading maritime museums, welcoming more than 2.5 million visitors each year. Set on Sydney’s waterfront, the Museum is a vibrant, inclusive and engaging place that brings stories to life and creates opportunities for discovery, learning and connection. 

ABOUT THE ROLE 

$33.05-$33.85 PER HOUR + SUPER 

This is not a role where you will simply watch from the sidelines. You will be right at the heart of the visitor experience. 

You will bring creativity, warmth and energy to family programs, activities and public events, helping children aged 0-14 and their carers explore, create, discover and have fun together. 

One day you might be facilitating a hands-on art or science activity in Kids on Deck or Mini Mariners. Another could see you supporting a creative workshop, underwater drone program, guided tour, Sensory Friendly day, performance or major Museum event. 

It is varied, hands-on and people-focused work, with the opportunity to create memorable experiences for families and visitors every day. 

WHAT'S ON OFFER? 

  • Flexible casual rostering to fit around your other commitments 
  • Training and development opportunities 
  • Staff wellbeing initiatives and sailing events 
  • A workplace that genuinely values diversity, inclusion and accessibility 
  • Penalty rates on Sundays and public holidays 
  • The chance to work in an extraordinary waterfront environment and be part of the experiences that bring the Museum to life 
WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

We are looking for people who genuinely enjoy engaging with others and know how to turn an activity, conversation or visit into a great experience. 

YOU'LL BRING: 

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills and confidence engaging with children, families and excursion groups 
  • Experience delivering engaging public programs in a museum or cultural setting 
  • Flexibility and adaptability to work across different activities, programs and environments 
  • Initiative and practical problem-solving skills, particularly when responding to visitor needs 
  • A genuine commitment to excellent customer service and the Museum’s values 
  • A collaborative approach and willingness to contribute to a positive and inclusive team 
  • Experience working with children and families, or studies in Early Childhood or Primary Education 
APPLICATIONS CLOSE AT 11.59 PM ON WEDNESDAY 25 NOVEMBER 2026. 

Please submit your resume and a short cover letter responding to the selection criteria by clicking APPLY. 

Australian citizenship is not required for these positions, as the role is engaged through a labour hire arrangement.

For more information, contact Gary Ward at Chandler Macleod on 02 7245 5361.

job.title: Geologist (Core Processing)
job.description:
Resource Geologist - Core Processing 
  • Competitive hourly pay range + super paid on all hours worked
  • 15/13 roster (days only) | FIFO from Perth
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto at Winu 
About the Opportunity 
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders. 
Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Resource Geologist to join the Resource Development team at Rio Tinto Winu. 
This is a great opportunity to join a safety-focused team working on site with Rio Tinto. You'll work alongside experienced crews, supporting day-to-day operations while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes. 
Reporting to the Specialist Resource Geology, your responsibilities will include: 
  • Processing and handling of diamond drill core in accordance with geological procedures and standards
  • Geologic logging of diamond core, including logging of observed structures, minerals and lithologies.  
  • Supporting daily geological and drilling activities across the core yard and field operations
  • Providing general geoscience support to the broader Resource Development team to ensure efficient, safe delivery of Rio Tinto’s Winu exploration programmes 
About You 
Proven experience working in dynamic exploration geology settings including core yard or exploration environments
  • Knowledge of intrusion-related copper-gold mineralisation styles or previous Paterson experience highly regarded
  • A positive attitude with a willingness to learn and contribute to a collaborative team environment
  • Strong data management and reporting skills with experience working in an office-based environment. Experience with AcQuire, ArcGIS Pro and Leapfrog highly desirable.
  • Hold a National Police Clearance (essential)
  • First Aid, Fire Attack and 4WD certification highly regarded
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills 
  • Dedication to everyone’s safety, including confidence to challenge unsafe work and stop the job when required 
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing 
Why Join Chandler Macleod? 
  • Competitive hourly pay range paid weekly
  • Superannuation paid on all hours worked
  • Consistent roster and work-life balance 
  • Opportunity to gain experience with Rio Tinto 
  • Dedicated Chandler Macleod support team 
  • Access to future opportunities across Rio Tinto operations 
Apply Now! 
Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading exploration operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

job.title: Completions Coordinator - HME
job.description:
Completions Coordinator - HME

Location: Perth CBD
Duration: 12-Month Contract
Start Date: Mid-December 2026
Roster: Monday to Friday (5:2)
Hours: 9 Hours Per Day

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Completions Coordinator - HME to support the successful delivery, commissioning and handover of Heavy Mobile Equipment (HME) project work packages.
Working closely with construction, commissioning, engineering, QA/QC, operations and vendor teams, you will be responsible for coordinating completions activities, managing documentation and certification requirements, and ensuring systems are ready for commissioning, acceptance and handover.
This is an excellent opportunity to join a major resources project in a Perth CBD-based role and contribute to the structured close-out and handover of critical HME assets.

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate HME completions activities to support commissioning and handover readiness.
  • Manage and maintain completions documentation, certificates and records.
  • Track and monitor Notices of Energisation (NOEs), Construction Verification Certificates (CVCs), Discipline Acceptance Certificates (DACs), Ready for Commissioning Certificates (RFCCs), Ready for Start-Up Certificates (RFSUs) and Inspection Release Certificates (IRCs).
  • Maintain completions trackers, registers, matrices and status reports.
  • Monitor Inspection and Test Records (ITRs), punch-list items, defects and outstanding actions through to close-out.
  • Prepare and distribute completions progress reports and status updates.
  • Liaise with engineering, construction, commissioning, QA/QC, operations and vendor stakeholders to resolve outstanding issues.
  • Monitor compliance with project completions and documentation requirements.
  • Identify and escalate risks, delays and barriers to commissioning readiness.
  • Support system handover, acceptance and project close-out activities.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Experience in completions, commissioning, project coordination or a similar role within mining, resources, heavy industry or major project environments.
  • Demonstrated experience managing completions documentation, certification and handover processes.
  • Strong understanding of completions workflows, including ITRs, punch lists, defects management and close-out requirements.
  • Experience working with HME, mobile equipment projects or related work packages highly regarded.
  • Solid document control, records management and traceability experience.
  • Strong proficiency maintaining trackers, registers and reporting tools.
  • Ability to coordinate across multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and completeness.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills with a collaborative approach.
What's on Offer
  • 12-month contract with potential for extension.
  • Perth CBD location.
  • Mid-December start.
  • Opportunity to contribute to a major mining and infrastructure project.
  • Collaborative team environment supporting a significant HME delivery program.
Apply now if you have a strong background in completions coordination, commissioning support, documentation management and project handover within complex industrial or resources projects.
job.salary: Super on all hours | Weekly pay

job.title: Hydrogeologist
job.description:
Hydrogeologist / Geologist 

NSW Locations | $85 per hour + Super | Contract to June 2027 

Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Hydrogeologist / Geologist for an exciting contract opportunity supporting environmental and project delivery outcomes across NSW. 

This role offers the opportunity to apply your technical expertise across a range of projects, providing specialist geological and hydrogeological advice, undertaking assessments and working with key stakeholders to deliver positive environmental outcomes. 

With multiple NSW office locations available and flexible hybrid working arrangements, this is an excellent opportunity for an experienced professional looking for their next contract assignment. 

The Opportunity 

You will provide specialist hydrogeological and geological expertise to support technical assessments, project delivery and environmental outcomes. 

Working across multiple projects and stakeholder groups, you'll be responsible for analysing technical information, preparing reports and delivering sound technical advice to support project objectives. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Provide hydrogeological and geological technical expertise across a range of projects. 

  • Undertake technical assessments, investigations, analysis and reporting. 

  • Review and interpret geological and hydrogeological information to support project decisions. 

  • Prepare clear, accurate technical reports, recommendations and advice. 

  • Engage with internal and external stakeholders to support project delivery. 

  • Manage competing priorities and deadlines across multiple projects. 

  • Contribute to environmental outcomes through high-quality technical assessments. 

About You 

To be successful in this role, you will bring: 

  • Tertiary qualifications in Hydrogeology, Geology or a closely related discipline. 

  • Demonstrated experience undertaking technical assessments, analysis and reporting. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. 

  • Excellent written communication and technical report-writing skills. 

  • Proven ability to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders. 

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines. 

  • Flexibility to work across different project requirements and stakeholder priorities. 

Experience working within environmental consulting, water resources, mining, infrastructure or government-related projects will be highly regarded. 

What's on Offer 

  • Hourly Rate: $85 per hour + superannuation. 

  • Contract Duration: 7 December 2026 to 30 June 2027. 

  • Working Hours: Average 35 hours per week, up to 40 hours maximum. 

  • Locations: Newcastle, Parramatta or Dubbo, with Wollongong and Wagga Wagga also available. 

  • Hybrid Working: Minimum two days per week in an NSW office, with flexibility required around attendance days. 

  • Opportunity to contribute to technically diverse projects across NSW. 

Important Information 

Applicants must currently reside in NSW and be able to attend an approved office location at least two days per week. 

The successful candidate will be required to complete relevant pre-employment checks. 

How to Apply 

If you're an experienced Hydrogeologist or Geologist seeking a new contract opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. 

Click Apply Now and submit your current resume outlining your relevant qualifications and technical experience. 

For a confidential discussion, contact Mark Seery, Senior Recruitment Consultant – Chandler Macleod. 

Applications are being reviewed immediately, so early applications are encouraged. 

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: A06 Senior Asset Accountant
job.description:
Our client, a QLD Government State Department, is looking to recruit a Senior Asset Accountant to join the team based in the Brisbane CBD.

The role will be responsible for, but not limited to:

  • Prepare and analyse monthly capital project reports, reconciliations, briefing notes, and presentations on a range of complex asset and capital management and budget issues, providing insights and recommendations to management
  • Contribute towards the development and review of capital management policies and procedures that will assist the agency to meet its obligations established under the Government’s financial management framework – legislation, guidelines and standards.
  • Provide accurate, professional and timely advice to Business Groups on asset policies for Capital Work-in-Progress, and associated acquisitions based on a good working knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards and Queensland Treasury Financial Reporting Requirements, Non-Current Asset Policies and other relevant policies.

job.title: Production Operator
job.description:
Warehouse Operator
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Warehouse Operator with a current forklift licence and proven high reach forklift experience to join our team. The purpose of this role is to prepare, move, and manage goods while providing efficient service to all transport providers and customers. The successful candidate will play a key role in maintaining safety, quality, inventory accuracy, and warehouse efficiency.
 
As a Warehouse Operator, you will play a key role in supporting our day-to-day warehouse operations, ensuring products are received, stored, picked, packed, and dispatched accurately while contributing to a safe and productive workplace.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Receive, inspect, and store incoming goods and materials.
  • Pick, pack, and prepare customer orders for dispatch.
  • Load and unload trucks using forklifts and warehouse equipment.
  • Operate RF scanners to manage inventory and stock movements.
  • Conduct stock counts and assist with inventory control activities.
  • Ensure stock is rotated and managed using FIFO principles.
  • Generate and apply labels to products and pallets as required.
  • Complete routine forklift inspections and report maintenance issues.
  • Maintain warehouse cleanliness and housekeeping standards.
  • Identify and report damaged stock, equipment faults, or safety concerns.
  • Follow all company policies, procedures, and safety requirements.
  • Assist with general warehouse duties and support the wider operations team as needed.
 
The Successful Applicant Will Have
  • Current Forklift Licence
  • High Reach Forklift experience (essential)
  • Previous experience in a warehouse, logistics, or manufacturing environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to perform manual handling tasks and work in a physically active role.
  • A strong commitment to workplace health and safety.
 Shift Details
  • Monday to Friday
  • 7:00am - 3:00pm
  • Overtime available as required
What's In It For You?
  • Competitive salary and stable full-time employment.
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment.
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities.
  • Safe, friendly, and inclusive workplace culture.
  • Work-life balance and employee wellbeing focus.
 
If you are a dependable team player with a positive attitude and a commitment to safety and quality, we would love to hear from you. Apply today to join our growing team.

job.title: Assistant Director - Strategy & Service Design
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Strategy and Initiatives Team sits within the Pathway and Digital Transformation Branch and plays a key role in shaping future services, experiences and organisational improvements across the Agency.
The team works across business areas to identify opportunities, solve complex challenges and support transformational initiatives that improve outcomes for participants, employees and stakeholders. Through strategic thinking, service design, research and collaboration, the team helps ensure the Agency's priorities are translated into practical and meaningful improvements.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Design Strategist to lead and contribute to strategic design, service design and organisational improvement initiatives.
Working in a complex and evolving environment, you will use human-centred design, systems thinking and strategic analysis to help solve complex problems, develop evidence-based recommendations and shape future service delivery approaches.
This role offers the opportunity to collaborate across the Agency, influence decision-making and contribute to initiatives that improve participant and staff experiences while delivering lasting organisational value.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead and contribute to strategic design, service design and organisational improvement initiatives.
  • Work in cross-functional teams to scope complex problems, understand user and operational needs, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Apply human-centred design, systems thinking and strategic analysis to develop practical solutions and recommendations.
  • Conduct research and analysis, synthesising qualitative and quantitative insights to support strategic decision-making.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across the Agency to shape future services, pathways, policies and operating models.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, presentations, business cases and recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Support the planning, development and implementation of transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Identify risks, opportunities and emerging trends that may impact future service delivery and organisational priorities.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience in strategy, service design, transformation, policy, innovation or organisational improvement within a complex environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems and translate insights into practical, evidence-based recommendations.
  • Experience applying human-centred design, systems thinking, research and analytical methodologies.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across diverse groups.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare documentation and presentations for senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to synthesise complex information into clear insights.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and delivering meaningful outcomes.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12- Month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Geelong VIC, Richmond VIC, Surry Hills NSW, Brisbane QLD, Deakin ACT, Adelaide SA, or Perth WA
  • $602.55 Daily + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.


Application closes on the 25th November 2026

job.title: Advisor Survey Delivery
job.description:
Advisor Survey Delivery
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto in Perth, Western Australia
  • 12-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
 
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders. Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Advisor Survey Delivery.  

Based in Central Park offices with the opportunity for ad hoc travel, this role offers the chance join a supportive team focused on safety, collaboration and delivering operational excellence within a leading global organisation, where you will be contributing to key operational and business outcomes.

Reporting to the Superintendent – Survey Delivery, you'll use your skills and experience to support business priorities, collaborate with key stakeholders and contribute to the success of the operation.

In this role, you will:  
  • Lead the delivery of biological surveys in remote areas of the Pilbara, with a strong focus on safety.
  • Plan and coordinate survey activities, including health and safety requirements, scheduling, site mobilisation and logistics for environmental consultants.
  • Apply Rio Tinto’s contractor management processes to support safe and effective survey delivery.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of survey delivery processes, including planning, coordination and field logistics.
  • Forecast accommodation requirements for the Biological Assessments team
  • Coordinate aviation requirements for helicopter-supported biological surveys, including engagement with aviation providers and operational readiness.
About You
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Practical problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to think on your feet and make sound decisions.
  • Interest in native flora and fauna and environmental approvals for Rio Tinto Iron Ore operations through the delivery of biological surveys in the Pilbara.
  • Experience using technical software, such as GIS or ArcGIS.
  • Dedication to everyone's safety.
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing.
 
Why Join Chandler Macleod?
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia's most experienced workforce partners. You'll receive a competitive hourly pay range paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.
 
Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading mining operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Diversity & Inclusion
Everyone is welcome at Chandler Macleod. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and inclusive teams. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, females, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and members of the LGBTIQA+ community. Together, we're creating workplaces where people feel they belong, can be themselves and have the opportunity to thrive.

job.title: Lead Electrical Commissioning Engineer
job.description:
Mission critical & data centre projects | Australian Citizenship required
Chandler Macleod is partnering with a leading global engineering and design consultancy to appoint a Lead Commissioning Engineer – Electrical to their growing Melbourne commissioning team.
You’ll lead electrical commissioning on some of Australia’s most complex projects across data centres, critical infrastructure, healthcare and building services. You’ll also be part of a respected international commissioning network.

About the role
This is a senior, hands-on leadership role. You’ll guide projects through the full commissioning lifecycle, coordinate stakeholders and testing, and make sure critical electrical systems are delivered safely, reliably and to design intent. You’ll be comfortable working independently and engaging with contractors, vendors, consultants, clients and facility operators.

Key responsibilities
  • Lead electrical commissioning across all project phases, from installation verification to integrated systems testing and handover
  • Prepare, review and implement Commissioning Management Plans, test procedures and documentation
  • Review contractor and vendor commissioning plans, test scripts and energisation plans
  • Lead FATs, FWTs, site inspections and functional performance testing
  • Lead Level 4 FPT and Level 5 IST
  • Troubleshoot complex electrical issues and drive resolution with stakeholders
  • Run commissioning workshops, meetings and technical reviews
  • Maintain issue registers, records and project reporting
  • Support planning, scheduling, risk management and commissioning readiness
  • Prepare and review commissioning reports and handover packages
  • Mentor junior commissioning engineers and help build team capability
  • Champion safety, quality and continuous improvement
Systems you’ll work across
  • LV and HV distribution
  • UPS, generators and backup power
  • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Switchboards, transformers and protection
  • Earthing and grounding
  • Fuel and emergency power systems
  • SCADA, EPMS and BMS
  • Integrated systems testing and operational readiness
About you
  • Tertiary qualification in Electrical or Building Services Engineering, or an electrical trade background with solid commissioning experience
  • Proven electrical commissioning experience on complex building services, mission critical, healthcare, industrial or infrastructure projects
  • Strong technical knowledge of critical power systems (LV/HV, UPS, generators, transformers, protection, SCADA, EPMS, BMS)
  • Experience writing and running commissioning plans, test procedures and integrated testing programs
  • Experience leading site-based commissioning through testing, troubleshooting and handover
  • Confident with clients and stakeholders, with strong written and verbal communication
  • Willing to travel to project sites as required
Highly regarded
  • Data centre, healthcare or other mission critical experience
  • Commissioning accreditations such as ACG CxA, CSA, BCxA, ASHRAE BCxP, Green Star AP or LEED
  • Experience with commissioning management systems and Microsoft Project
Essential requirement
Australian Citizenship is mandatory. You must also be eligible to obtain and maintain an Australian Government Baseline Security Clearance, with the ability to obtain higher levels if required.

What’s on offer
  • Exposure to technically challenging, nationally significant projects
  • Career development, mentoring and training through a global commissioning network
  • A collaborative, multidisciplinary team that values technical excellence
  • An inclusive workplace that supports its people to grow

job.title: Hydrogeologist
job.description:
Hydrogeologist / Geologist 

NSW Locations | $85 per hour + Super | Contract to June 2027 

Chandler Macleod is seeking an experienced Hydrogeologist / Geologist for an exciting contract opportunity supporting environmental and project delivery outcomes across NSW. 

This role offers the opportunity to apply your technical expertise across a range of projects, providing specialist geological and hydrogeological advice, undertaking assessments and working with key stakeholders to deliver positive environmental outcomes. 

With multiple NSW office locations available and flexible hybrid working arrangements, this is an excellent opportunity for an experienced professional looking for their next contract assignment. 

The Opportunity 

You will provide specialist hydrogeological and geological expertise to support technical assessments, project delivery and environmental outcomes. 

Working across multiple projects and stakeholder groups, you'll be responsible for analysing technical information, preparing reports and delivering sound technical advice to support project objectives. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Provide hydrogeological and geological technical expertise across a range of projects. 

  • Undertake technical assessments, investigations, analysis and reporting. 

  • Review and interpret geological and hydrogeological information to support project decisions. 

  • Prepare clear, accurate technical reports, recommendations and advice. 

  • Engage with internal and external stakeholders to support project delivery. 

  • Manage competing priorities and deadlines across multiple projects. 

  • Contribute to environmental outcomes through high-quality technical assessments. 

About You 

To be successful in this role, you will bring: 

  • Tertiary qualifications in Hydrogeology, Geology or a closely related discipline. 

  • Demonstrated experience undertaking technical assessments, analysis and reporting. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. 

  • Excellent written communication and technical report-writing skills. 

  • Proven ability to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders. 

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines. 

  • Flexibility to work across different project requirements and stakeholder priorities. 

Experience working within environmental consulting, water resources, mining, infrastructure or government-related projects will be highly regarded. 

What's on Offer 

  • Hourly Rate: $85 per hour + superannuation. 

  • Contract Duration: 7 December 2026 to 30 June 2027. 

  • Working Hours: Average 35 hours per week, up to 40 hours maximum. 

  • Locations: Newcastle, Parramatta or Dubbo, with Wollongong and Wagga Wagga also available. 

  • Hybrid Working: Minimum two days per week in an NSW office, with flexibility required around attendance days. 

  • Opportunity to contribute to technically diverse projects across NSW. 

Important Information 

Applicants must currently reside in NSW and be able to attend an approved office location at least two days per week. 

The successful candidate will be required to complete relevant pre-employment checks. 

How to Apply 

If you're an experienced Hydrogeologist or Geologist seeking a new contract opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. 

Click Apply Now and submit your current resume outlining your relevant qualifications and technical experience. 

For a confidential discussion, contact Mark Seery, Senior Recruitment Consultant – Chandler Macleod. 

Applications are being reviewed immediately, so early applications are encouraged.

job.title: Assistant Director - Strategy & Service Design
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Strategy and Initiatives Team sits within the Pathway and Digital Transformation Branch and plays a key role in shaping future services, experiences and organisational improvements across the Agency.
The team works across business areas to identify opportunities, solve complex challenges and support transformational initiatives that improve outcomes for participants, employees and stakeholders. Through strategic thinking, service design, research and collaboration, the team helps ensure the Agency's priorities are translated into practical and meaningful improvements.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Design Strategist to lead and contribute to strategic design, service design and organisational improvement initiatives.
Working in a complex and evolving environment, you will use human-centred design, systems thinking and strategic analysis to help solve complex problems, develop evidence-based recommendations and shape future service delivery approaches.
This role offers the opportunity to collaborate across the Agency, influence decision-making and contribute to initiatives that improve participant and staff experiences while delivering lasting organisational value.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead and contribute to strategic design, service design and organisational improvement initiatives.
  • Work in cross-functional teams to scope complex problems, understand user and operational needs, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Apply human-centred design, systems thinking and strategic analysis to develop practical solutions and recommendations.
  • Conduct research and analysis, synthesising qualitative and quantitative insights to support strategic decision-making.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across the Agency to shape future services, pathways, policies and operating models.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, presentations, business cases and recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Support the planning, development and implementation of transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Identify risks, opportunities and emerging trends that may impact future service delivery and organisational priorities.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience in strategy, service design, transformation, policy, innovation or organisational improvement within a complex environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems and translate insights into practical, evidence-based recommendations.
  • Experience applying human-centred design, systems thinking, research and analytical methodologies.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across diverse groups.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare documentation and presentations for senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and deliver outcomes in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to synthesise complex information into clear insights.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and delivering meaningful outcomes.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12- Month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Geelong VIC, Richmond VIC, Surry Hills NSW, Brisbane QLD, Deakin ACT, Adelaide SA, or Perth WA
  • $602.55 Daily + Super

job.title: Poultry Farm Manager
job.description:
Baiada is seeking an experienced Poultry Farm Manager to lead day-to-day farm operations and ensure production targets are met while maintaining the highest standards across animal welfare, biosecurity, food safety, and workplace safety. This is a hands-on leadership role suited to someone who enjoys operational ownership and leading teams in a fast-paced farming environment.

About the Client
Passionate about producing premium quality poultry products through the Lilydale Free Range and Steggles brands, our client Baiada has been bringing Australian families together at the dinner table since 1919.
As one of Australia's largest poultry producers, Baiada is committed to maintaining the highest standards of animal welfare, biosecurity, safety, and operational excellence across its farming and processing operations.

About the Role
As the Farm Manager, you will be responsible for the overall management of day-to-day farm operations, ensuring production targets are achieved while maintaining animal welfare, biosecurity, safety, and company standards. This position requires strong leadership, operational planning, and a hands-on approach to farm management.
  • Take responsibility for the overall performance and operation of the farm
  • Lead and supervise the farm team, ensuring work is completed safely and efficiently
  • Monitor bird health, welfare, and farm conditions to achieve optimum production results
  • Ensure all biosecurity and animal welfare requirements are consistently maintained
  • Oversee daily farm activities, including shed checks, bird placements, and flock management
  • Maintain accurate production, performance, and compliance records
  • Ensure farm equipment, sheds, and facilities are maintained to a high standard
  • Drive a positive safety culture and ensure compliance with WHS requirements
  • Work closely with management and technical teams to achieve farm objectives
  • Identify and address operational issues as they arise
  • Manage farm resources effectively to support production targets
  • Ensure all company policies, procedures, and standards are followed

Skills & Experience:
To be successful in this role, you will:
  • Have previous experience in poultry, livestock, or agricultural farm management
  • Demonstrate strong leadership and people management skills
  • Have a sound understanding of animal welfare and biosecurity requirements
  • Be capable of making operational decisions and working independently
  • Possess strong communication, organisational, and problem-solving skills
  • Have experience with record keeping and basic computer-based reporting systems
  • Understand Workplace Health and Safety requirements and compliance obligations
  • Hold relevant agricultural or livestock qualifications (desirable but not essential)
  • Be reliable, proactive, and committed to achieving operational targets

Why Join Baiada?
  • Join one of Australia's leading poultry producers
  • Lead a dedicated and supportive team
  • Work in a role that offers responsibility, autonomy, and career growth
  • Be part of an organisation committed to safety, animal welfare, and continuous improvement

If you are an experienced agricultural leader looking for your next challenge, we would love to hear from you.

How to Apply
Click APPLY or contact the Baiada Recruitment Team on 02 6762 9055 or baiadahanwood@chandlermacleod.com for a confidential discussion.

Apply now, including your relevant food mixing experience and preferred shift availability.

job.title: Onsite Consultant
job.description:
About the role
We’re looking for an experienced and people-focused Onsite Consultant to support a large casual workforce within a busy, high-volume distribution operation. This is a hands-on role where you’ll be the go-to person for approximately 200 casual employees, providing day-to-day support, managing attendance and performance, monitoring workplace standards and ensuring the workforce runs smoothly throughout the night shift.

You’ll play a key role in maintaining workforce engagement, addressing employee concerns and working closely with operational stakeholders to ensure staffing requirements and expectations are met.

This is a permanent, full-time opportunity offering a $90,000 inclusive salary, working a 7-day rotating roster across a 5:30pm–4:30am shift. 

Roster:
  • Week 1: Wednesday – Saturday
  • Week 2: Thursday – Saturday

Duties
  • Act as the primary point of contact for a large casual workforce of approximately 200 employees
  • Monitor daily attendance, absenteeism, punctuality and workforce coverage
  • Manage employee performance, conduct and behavioural concerns, escalating issues where required
  • Monitor workplace hygiene, presentation and compliance with site standards
  • Build strong working relationships with employees, providing ongoing support and guidance
  • Manage employee queries, concerns and day-to-day workplace issues
  • Liaise with operational stakeholders regarding workforce requirements, performance and productivity
  • Maintain accurate employee records, reporting and workforce documentation
  • Assist with onboarding, inductions and general employee administration

Skills and experience
  • Previous experience in recruitment, workforce coordination, onsite recruitment, HR, rostering or people management
  • Confident managing a large workforce, ideally within warehousing, logistics, manufacturing or high-volume operations
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport across all levels
  • Ability to manage challenging conversations and address performance or attendance issues confidently
  • Highly organised with strong administration and time management skills
  • Resilient and adaptable, with the ability to juggle competing priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable working independently and making decisions within a night shift environment

Benefits
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Structured rotating roster with regular days off
  • Join an established onsite recruitment and workforce management team

job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:
HR Business Partner
Casual role duration: 16 Nov – 3 Feb 2027
Start: ASAP
Location: South Australia
Salary: ASO6 equivalent 
About the Role
We’re seeking an experienced HR Business Partner undertakes work under broad direction in the management and delivery of a significant human resource management service which targets current and future organisational needs. This requires working closely with business leaders and/or line managers to identify and achieve shared organisational objectives.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide strategic HR services to ensure the achievement of operational business goals. 
  • Provide expert human resource advice to leaders and staff.
  • Support workforce planning and strategy development
  • Ensure continuous improvement across the HR function
  • Build strong relationships with managers and staff.
About You

  • Demonstrated leadership and management skills to motivate and influence others in an environment of change, understand interpersonal conflict, identify effective strategies for resolution and support line management to achieve positive outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and sustain effective collaborative working relationships and business partnerships with clients.
  • Demonstrated professional integrity and competence that contributes to the achievement of objectives.
  • Demonstrated effective verbal communication and negotiation skills and ability to liaise with all levels to influence outcomes and gain support and commitment.
  • Demonstrated effective writing skills and ability to prepare complex reports that highlight options and risk for Executive on complex and politically sensitive issues.
  • Proven ability to analyse and solve complex situations and problems, and apply practical people management and solutions to achieve business outcomes.

Experience
  • Demonstrated experience in providing leadership in HR and people management issues.
  • Proven experience planning, developing and implementing changes to procedures/systems within and across work groups.
  • Experience in advising management in the training and development of staff.
  • Delivering effective human resource services including providing complex advice on strategic and operational matters.
  • Experience interpreting awards, legislation and policies, and applying them successfully to deliver business outcomes.
  • Must have SA Public Sector experience, Ideally Health experience

Knowledge
  • Possess a sound understanding of contemporary HR practices and approaches, human resource management and procedures and their application with the SA Public Sector, including awards, guidelines, EB Agreements and Codes of Practice, WHS, EEO and performance management processes and quality improvement Seniors and procedures.
  • Possess a sound understanding of the impact of change and organisational development methodologies.

Compliance Requirements
National Police Check and relevant DHS screenings.

job.title: Internal Review Officer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Internal Review Officer to undertake reviews of decisions relating to participant access, eligibility, and funded supports.
This role is suited to professionals who enjoy analysing complex information, interpreting legislation and policy, and making evidence-based recommendations. You will manage a caseload of review matters while ensuring decisions are completed accurately, within required timeframes, and in line with legislative and operational requirements.
The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical skills, attention to detail, sound judgement, and a commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Undertake internal reviews by gathering, assessing, and analysing information and evidence.
  • Apply relevant legislation, policy, operational guidelines, and procedures to support fair and consistent recommendations.
  • Prepare clear, objective, and well-reasoned review findings and recommendations.
  • Communicate review outcomes, review rights, and appeal pathways in a professional and timely manner.
  • Engage with participants, representatives, and stakeholders to obtain information and support informed decision-making.
  • Manage a caseload of review matters while meeting legislative and operational timeframes.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation to support compliant and defensible review processes.
  • Apply person-centred, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive approaches when dealing with sensitive matters.
  • Contribute to quality assurance activities, continuous improvement initiatives, and service delivery enhancements.
  • Maintain knowledge of relevant legislation, policy, and operational frameworks.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, procedures, or regulatory frameworks.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyse information and evidence to develop logical, balanced, and defensible recommendations.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to make sound decisions based on available information.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, findings, recommendations, or assessments.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and caseloads within established timeframes.
  • Ability to manage sensitive or complex matters using sound judgement and professionalism.
  • Strong organisational skills and experience maintaining accurate records and case documentation.
  • Commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes and high-quality customer service.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment while managing individual responsibilities.

Highly Desirable
  • Experience within government, administrative review, regulatory, disability, health, community services, or human services environments.
  • Knowledge of administrative review processes and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Experience assessing complex information and preparing recommendations in a legislative or policy-driven environment.
  • Knowledge of disability, functional impact, or participant-centred service delivery models.
  • Experience using case management, customer relationship management (CRM), or workflow management systems.
  • Qualifications in Law, Public Administration, Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Disability Studies, or a related discipline.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • $55.24 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.



Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.description:

We are seeking an organised and proactive Rostering Coordinator to join a busy distribution centre team. This is a fast-paced, time-critical role responsible for coordinating daily workforce requirements and ensuring shifts are adequately staffed.

Using internal rostering systems, you will manage shift allocations, respond to last-minute cancellations and quickly source replacements to minimise staffing gaps. This role will suit someone who thrives under pressure, enjoys problem-solving and can think on their feet.

  • Communicate roster changes and shift requirements to employees.
  • Respond to staffing issues quickly and effectively in a high-volume environment.
  • Maintain accurate rostering records and update internal systems.

Skills and Experience
  • Previous experience in rostering, workforce coordination, scheduling or high-volume administration.

  • Highly organised, proactive and comfortable making quick decisions.
  • Flexible and adaptable, with a strong focus on ensuring operational requirements are met.

  • Consistent 4-day working week.

job.title: Workforce Coordinator/Onsite Consultant
job.description:
Onsite Consultant

Are you passionate about client success and operational excellence? Join our team as an Onsite Consultant dedicated to supporting a national client of Chandler Macleod.

This critical role offers a unique opportunity to be at the forefront of our partnership with one of the world's most innovative companies. Making a real impact on the day-to-day warehouse operations, you will manage a casual workforce through performance, safety and feedback whilst ensuring seamless communication between clients and teams.

What You’ll Do:
  • Act as the primary onsite point of contact working alongside the operations teams to coordinate and manage the casual workforce to ensure staffing levels meet operational demands and SLA expectations.
  • Support onboarding and mobilisation of casual workers, monitor attendance, roster adherence, and workforce performance standards, escalating issues where required.
  • Maintain strong relationships with workers through regular check-ins to support and improve engagement, retention, and overall workforce experience.
  • Assist with performance management processes by documenting and communicating performance or conduct concerns to relevant stakeholders.
  • Support payroll administration processes by ensuring accurate attendance and roster records are maintained.
  • Support peak periods and changing operational requirements through flexibility in working hours where required.
  • Meet site compliance and provide regular reporting on key operational metrics including zero hours, attendance, roster compliance, productivity, and engagement.
Drawing upon your experience in either workforce coordination, onsite consulting, labour hire recruitment, or operations support environments, you will have:
  • Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities, changing operational and client needs within a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Confidence in communicating with key stakeholders and the ability to build strong working relationships with clients, employees, and internal teams.
  • Experience in handling workforce-related issues professionally and a thorough understanding of workplace safety and compliance requirements.
  • Precise attention to detail and accuracy in reporting with proficiency in performing administrative tasks within Microsoft Office and workforce management systems.
  • Flexibility to support shift coverage which may span across 4am – 3pm and may include public holidays.

If you're interested to play an important role in ensuring effective workforce coordination, service delivery, and positive engagement outcomes for our client, we welcome you to APPLY BELOW.

job.title: Live Bay Process Worker
job.description:
Join us as a Live Bay Process Worker! No experience needed!

We are currently seeking process workers to join Baiada’s team in their live bay area at the Beresfield processing facility. This facility is designed to meet the highest standards of food safety and quality, whilst also ensuring the welfare of their chickens and turkeys.

The successful candidates will be responsible for hanging live birds on the processing line and performing evisceration duties in a safe and efficient manner.


About the Role:
  • Hanging live birds on the processing line for start of production
  • Performing evisceration duties, including removing internal organs of the birds
  • Inspecting birds for defects or abnormalities and removing any birds that do not meet quality standards
  • Maintaining a clean and safe working environment in accordance with hygiene and safety standards.
  • Start times as early as 3-4am

Skills & Experience:
  • We value reliability and punctuality above all else. If you have a proven attendance record and can commit to working 5 days per week, we want to hear from you!
  • Manual handling and repetitive lifting are part of the job, so if you have physical restrictions then this role may not be for you
  • If you have a reliable method of transport and full working rights in Australia, you’re eligible to apply!

Benefits:
  • Competitive hourly rates starting from $32.81 per hour plus allowances
  • No weekend work
  • Immediate starts!
  • Enjoy secure parking and our canteen facilities

job.title: Onsite Manager
job.description:
About the role
We’re looking for a senior on-site leader to manage a large casual workforce at a flagship fulfilment / distribution operation in Cranbourne. This is a high-impact operational leadership position where you’ll bring calm structure to a fast-moving environment, use data to make confident decisions, and lead from the front.
 
This role is on-site Monday–Friday, typically 9:00am–5:00pm, with occasional after-hours availability for escalations (not frequent, but can happen due to 24/7 operations). Start ASAP in a permanent, full time role. 
 
 
Duties
  • Lead and develop a team of approximately 12 direct reports within an established on-site operation
  • Oversee day-to-day workforce performance across high-volume warehousing functions (pick/pack, forklift, general warehouse operations)
  • Support workforce planning, rostering and coordination to meet operational requirements
  • Partner with key stakeholders to ensure workforce capability, engagement and productivity outcomes are met
  • Use data and reporting to identify trends, drive decisions, and support continuous improvement
  • Manage escalations professionally and maintain stability under pressure in a dynamic environment
 
Skills and experience
  • Strong experience leading teams in warehousing, logistics, distribution, manufacturing or high-volume operations
  • Proven ability to use data to drive decisions (comfortable with KPIs, reporting, performance trends)
  • Confident communicator with strong stakeholder management and customer/service mindset
  • Calm, leadership style with high emotional intelligence and people focus
  • Decisive and outcomes-driven; able to operate effectively in imperfect / changing environments
 
Desirable:
  • Exposure to 24/7 operations and large casual workforces
  • Experience in continuous improvement / operational uplift environments
 
Benefits
  • Permanent role with a well-established on-site team
  • Senior leadership opportunity in a large-scale, fast-paced operation
  • Strong career progression opportunities 

How to apply

job.title: School Crossing Supervisor City of Monash
job.description:
Start the New Year with a Role That Makes a Real Difference in Your Community

Are you looking for meaningful, part-time work that fits seamlessly around your lifestyle and offers excellent work–life balance? If so, our School Crossing Supervisor role could be the perfect opportunity for you.

As a School Crossing Supervisor, you will play a vital role in keeping school-aged children, families, and pedestrians safe during busy morning and afternoon school times. This is a rewarding position where you’ll become a familiar and trusted face in your local community.

Positions are available across the City of Monash, with placements offered as close to your home as possible based on operational requirements and availability.

About the role
  • Assist children and pedestrians to safely cross the road during peak school hours

To be successful, you will
  • Be friendly, reliable, community-minded, and confident communicating with people of all ages

What’s in it for you?

  • Consistent hours that support work–life balance

If you’re ready to start a role that’s rewarding, flexible, and community focused, we’d love to hear from you.
