job.title: Senior Case Manager (Administrative Review Tribunal)
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Case Manager to manage a portfolio of complex review matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
This role requires a highly organised professional who can exercise sound judgement, navigate complex issues, and build strong stakeholder relationships. You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of cases, identifying resolution pathways, gathering and analysing information, and contributing to positive outcomes through effective case management and dispute resolution practices.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Manage end-to-end case management activities for matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
  • Analyse complex information and develop options to support early and effective resolution.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Obtain, assess, and interpret evidence to support decision-making and case outcomes.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, correspondence, reports, and case management documentation.
  • Attend and participate in Case Conferences, Conciliations, and Hearings.
  • Apply negotiation, advocacy, and dispute resolution techniques to resolve matters efficiently.
  • Identify, assess, and respond to risks impacting participants, operational outcomes, and business objectives.
  • Manage competing priorities and meet legislated and operational timeframes.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and best-practice case management approaches.


You Must Have
 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, sensitive, or high-risk cases.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective working relationships.
  • Proven analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to make sound decisions.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing detailed reports, briefs, or recommendations.
  • Strong verbal communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume and deadline-driven environment.
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, or procedural frameworks.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to exercise professional judgement in complex situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team while managing an independent caseload
  • Experience with administrative law, merits review, tribunal, or appeals processes.
  • Experience within disability, health, community services, government, or social services environments.
  • Experience in insurance claims, underwriting, actuarial services, or compensation schemes.
  • Experience in dispute resolution, investigations, complaints handling, or regulatory case management.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • $60.26 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.title: Assistant Director - Information Governance and Records Management
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced Information Governance and Records Management to lead information governance, records management and compliance initiatives within a complex, fast-paced and high-profile environment—contributing to a nationally significant program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within a major Federal Government program environment, you will be accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for leading one of the organisation’s specialist information management streams and delivering strategic outcomes across information governance, records management, and/or records authority development.

You will strengthen information management capability, promote a culture of accountability and compliance, and deliver enterprise-wide frameworks, services and assurance activities that ensure information is managed effectively, securely and in accordance with legislative requirements.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering information governance and records management outcomes, including:
  • Leading information governance, records management and compliance initiatives across a large, complex program environment
  • Developing and implementing information governance frameworks, policies, procedures, guidance and assurance activities
  • Providing expert, evidence-based advice to senior leaders and stakeholders to support informed decision-making
  • Driving improvements to information lifecycle management practices, including compliance monitoring and reporting obligations
  • Overseeing and optimising Electronic Document and Records Management System (EDRMS) usage, support and service delivery
  • Leading or contributing to records authority development, sentencing methodologies, and compliant retention and disposal practices
  • Identifying, assessing and managing risk, escalating issues appropriately, and delivering practical mitigation strategies
  • Building and leading a high-performing team, including capability uplift, performance management and fostering a collaborative culture
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and recommendations that clearly outline issues, impacts, options and next steps
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Strong knowledge of information governance, records management and information lifecycle management within legislative and policy frameworks (including the Archives Act 1983)
  • Proven ability to translate strategic direction, technical concepts and legislative requirements into clear, practical deliverables
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to influence and collaborate across diverse internal and external groups
  • Demonstrated leadership capability, with experience leading teams and coordinating complex work programs to achieve outcomes
  • Sound judgement, initiative and accountability, with the ability to operate effectively in a high-paced environment
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce high-quality executive briefs and advice

Security RequirementApplicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 2 (NV2) security clearance.
Flexible working arrangements may be supported where aligned with operational and business requirements.

Locations:
Adelaide SA, Canberra/ACT (Majura), Rockingham WA

Apply Now
If you are an experienced information governance and records management leader seeking to contribute to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today.

  • Experience using SQL for querying, extracting and analysing data.

job.title: Haul Truck Operator
job.description:

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced CAT 777 Dump Truck Operator to support day-to-day mining operations in the Gove region, NT.

This is a great opportunity to join a safety-focused team working on site with Rio Tinto. You'll work alongside experienced crews, supporting production targets while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes.

Reporting to the site Supervisor, your responsibilities will include:

  • Demonstrated experience operating CAT 777 (or similar mining haul trucks)

job.title: Mobilisation Coordinator
job.description:
Mobilisation Coordinator | Mining & Resources
Drive Workforce Readiness Across Major Mining and Resources Operations

About the Role We are seeking a highly organised and outcome-driven Mobilisation Coordinator to take responsibility for the successful mobilisation of employees and contractors across mining, resources and construction projects.

This role goes beyond administration. You will be accountable for ensuring personnel meet all client and company requirements, are fully compliant, and arrive on site ready to commence as scheduled.

Success in this role requires strong ownership, attention to detail, and the ability to drive mobilisation activities through to completion.
You will actively manage competing priorities, identify risks early, engage stakeholders, and remove obstacles to achieve mobilisation outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Take ownership of the mobilisation process from placement through to successful site commencement.
  • Drive mobilisation activities to ensure all personnel meet project deadlines and client onboarding requirements.
  • Coordinate and monitor pre-employment medicals, drug and alcohol testing, inductions, training, and site access requirements.
  • Verify licences, qualifications, trade certificates, competencies, and compliance documentation to ensure workforce readiness.
  • Coordinate travel, accommodation, roster movements, and logistics where required.
  • Maintain accurate mobilisation and compliance records within workforce management systems.
  • Monitor progress against commencement schedules and actively follow up outstanding requirements.
  • Build strong working relationships with candidates, recruiters, operational leaders, clients, training providers, and medical providers.
  • Identify mobilisation risks, compliance issues, or delays and take proactive action to achieve mobilisation outcomes.
  • Escalate critical issues appropriately while maintaining ownership of resolution activities.
  • Provide accurate mobilisation reporting and status updates to stakeholders.
  • Support workforce planning and mobilisation forecasting to meet operational requirements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance mobilisation efficiency, candidate experience, and compliance performance.
About You You are someone who takes ownership, follows through on commitments, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where meeting mobilisation deadlines is critical.

You will bring:

  • Experience in workforce mobilisation, onboarding, recruitment coordination, workforce administration, or a similar role within mining, resources, construction, energy, or industrial sectors.
  • A proven ability to manage multiple mobilisations simultaneously while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
  • Strong accountability and a track record of delivering outcomes against tight timeframes.
  • Experience coordinating medicals, training, site inductions, compliance checks, and workforce logistics.
  • The confidence to engage stakeholders, challenge delays, and drive actions to completion.
  • Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Experience using recruitment, HR, mobilisation, or workforce management systems.
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach with the ability to anticipate issues before they impact commencement dates.
Desirable Experience
  • Mobilising personnel to FIFO, project, maintenance, or operational mining environments.
  • Working with major mining and resources clients and their onboarding requirements.
  • Coordinating high-volume workforce mobilisation programs across multiple sites.
Why Join Us?
  • Play a critical role in delivering workforce outcomes across major mining and resource projects.
  • Join a high-performing team that values accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Work in a role where your ability to drive outcomes has a direct impact on operational success.
  • Build your career in a dynamic and growing workforce solutions environment.

job.title: Senior Pricing Policy Adviser (Economics)
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

The Agency is responsible for delivering critical reforms and policy initiatives that support the effective operation and long-term sustainability of the NDIS. The team works at the centre of complex policy, pricing and regulatory programs, providing strategic advice and evidence-based recommendations that influence decision-making across the organisation and government. The Agency is seeking an experienced policy professional to support the development and implementation of pricing policy initiatives and reform programs. job.title: Transition Manager
job.description:
Are you an experienced Transition Manager who thrives in complex enterprise environments and enjoys turning large-scale technology programs into sustainable operational success?
We're seeking a highly capable Transition Manager to play a pivotal role in one of Australia's most significant retail transformation initiatives. This opportunity will see you leading the transition of critical technology platforms, services and operating capabilities from program delivery into business-as-usual operations, ensuring customer outcomes, operational stability and long-term success. This is a 12 month contract role in Melbourne CBD in a hybrid working environment with our client AGL.

About the Role
As the Transition Manager, you will own the end-to-end transition strategy and execution across a complex portfolio of technology initiatives.
You will be responsible for ensuring new platforms, services and capabilities are successfully embedded into operational teams, with a strong focus on governance, readiness, knowledge transfer, risk management, service acceptance and post-go-live stabilisation.
Working within a major Retail Transformation program, you'll become the central point of coordination between delivery teams, operational support functions, business stakeholders and third-party partners.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and execute end-to-end transition strategies, roadmaps and integrated transition plans
  • Drive operational readiness activities across multiple technology releases and transformation streams
  • Lead transition planning through mobilisation, go-live, hypercare, stabilisation and handover
  • Establish governance frameworks, readiness gates, service acceptance criteria and success measures
  • Coordinate knowledge transfer activities across technical, operational and service-management teams
  • Manage transition risks, dependencies, issues and critical path activities
  • Partner with architecture, operations, cybersecurity, service management, vendors and delivery teams
  • Lead readiness and service acceptance forums and provide executive-level reporting and recommendations
  • Ensure support models, operating procedures, monitoring, incident management and vendor arrangements are fully established prior to handover
  • Drive continuous improvement and transition best practices across the broader transformation program
About You
You are a seasoned Transition Manager with a proven track record delivering complex technology and operational transitions within large-scale enterprise transformation programs.
You'll bring strong stakeholder management capabilities, the ability to influence at executive level, and experience navigating highly regulated environments with multiple delivery partners.

Essential Experience
  • Significant experience managing large-scale technology transitions within enterprise organisations
  • Experience across regulated industries such as Energy, Utilities, Financial Services, Telecommunications or similar sectors
  • Proven background transitioning SaaS platforms and integrated technology ecosystems
  • Experience working across environments involving:
    • Salesforce
    • Digital platforms and customer channels
    • Integration platforms
    • Billing and payments systems
    • Cloud and data platforms
  • Strong knowledge of operational readiness, service acceptance, hypercare and business handover processes
  • Experience working with managed service providers, outsourcing partners or global delivery models
  • Strong programme governance, reporting and stakeholder management capability
If you're passionate about delivering successful technology transitions and have the experience to lead complex enterprise change into sustainable operations, please click APPLY NOW and follow the prompts.

job.title: Senior Case Manager (Administrative Review Tribunal)
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Case Manager to manage a portfolio of complex review matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
This role requires a highly organised professional who can exercise sound judgement, navigate complex issues, and build strong stakeholder relationships. You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of cases, identifying resolution pathways, gathering and analysing information, and contributing to positive outcomes through effective case management and dispute resolution practices.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Manage end-to-end case management activities for matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
  • Analyse complex information and develop options to support early and effective resolution.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Obtain, assess, and interpret evidence to support decision-making and case outcomes.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, correspondence, reports, and case management documentation.
  • Attend and participate in Case Conferences, Conciliations, and Hearings.
  • Apply negotiation, advocacy, and dispute resolution techniques to resolve matters efficiently.
  • Identify, assess, and respond to risks impacting participants, operational outcomes, and business objectives.
  • Manage competing priorities and meet legislated and operational timeframes.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and best-practice case management approaches.


You Must Have
 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, sensitive, or high-risk cases.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective working relationships.
  • Proven analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to make sound decisions.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing detailed reports, briefs, or recommendations.
  • Strong verbal communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume and deadline-driven environment.
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, or procedural frameworks.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to exercise professional judgement in complex situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team while managing an independent caseload
  • Experience with administrative law, merits review, tribunal, or appeals processes.
  • Experience within disability, health, community services, government, or social services environments.
  • Experience in insurance claims, underwriting, actuarial services, or compensation schemes.
  • Experience in dispute resolution, investigations, complaints handling, or regulatory case management.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • $60.26 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.title: Chef
job.description:
Looking for a new and exciting opportunity with a global catering giant?

Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Chefs to join a dynamic team within a large catering facility in Tullamarine.

Our client is a leading food manufacturer, producing meals to many of the worlds' major Airlines.

In this role, you will be responsible for producing high‑volume, in‑flight meals for airline passengers while maintaining consistent quality standards in a fast‑paced commercial kitchen.

This is a casual position offering full‑time hours, with opportunities for permanent progression.
  • Day Shift: 7:00 AM start 
  • Afternoon Shift: 3:00 PM start 
Key Responsibilities:
  • Prepare, cook, and assemble food in line with client and flight specifications, including dietary requirements.
  • Follow written instructions/ recipes 
  • Repetitive lifting and manual handling up to 25kg
  • Maintain and adhere to HACCP and OHS policies and standards. 
  • Work under tight time constraints to meet KPIs and scheduling changes
  • Manage food production, including stock levels and quantities
  • Conduct quality control checks throughout production
  • Supervise and coordinate the work of Catering Assistants

To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • A Certificate III and IV in Commercial Cookery
  • Recent experience in a food manufacturing or high-volume kitchen environment
  • Successfully complete a 2 hour trial onsite
  • Flexibility to work a rotating roster.
  • Availability for on-call shifts or overtime as required
  • Reliable transportation and a valid driver’s license
  • Full working rights and availability in Australia
  • Strong work ethic, reliability, and initiative
  • A passion for food and customer satisfaction

This is a fantastic career opportunity for a motivated individual to grow their career with a market leader.
If this sounds like you, apply now!

job.title: Data Insights and Reporting Analyst
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Data Insights and Reporting Analyst to support a high-profile national service delivery function. This is an excellent opportunity for a data-driven professional with strong analytical, reporting and stakeholder engagement skills to contribute to operational excellence and improved customer outcomes within a large government environment.

About the Role
As an Data Insights and Reporting Analyst, you will be part of a Strategy and Analytics team responsible for delivering meaningful insights, performance reporting and data visualisations that support operational and strategic decision-making. You will work with large and complex datasets to identify trends, uncover opportunities for improvement and provide actionable recommendations to stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and deliver performance reports, dashboards and data visualisations using a range of reporting tools and analytical techniques.
  • Analyse customer and operational data to identify trends, patterns and performance drivers.
  • Build meaningful insights that support evidence-based decision-making across business areas.
  • Design and maintain dashboards that provide clear visibility of operational performance.
  • Transform, cleanse and model data from multiple sources to support reporting and analytics requirements.
  • Conduct statistical and trend analysis to identify service improvement opportunities.
  • Prepare high-quality reporting and presentations for senior stakeholders and executive audiences.
  • Ensure data governance, integrity and reporting standards are maintained.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to understand reporting requirements and deliver fit-for-purpose solutions.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance service delivery and customer experience.

About You To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience developing reports, dashboards and data visualisations that support business performance and decision-making.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex datasets and communicate insights effectively.
  • Experience working with business intelligence and reporting tools such as Power BI or similar platforms.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including data modelling, Power Query and reporting capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving, critical thinking and decision-making capabilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver outcomes within tight deadlines.
  • Experience working in dynamic, fast-paced operational environments.

Highly Desirable
  • Experience using SQL for querying, extracting and analysing data.
  • Experience working with customer service, contact centre or high-volume service delivery environments.
  • Experience with data visualisation and business intelligence platforms such as Power BI.
  • Knowledge of data modelling, reporting frameworks and performance analysis methodologies.
  • Experience presenting insights and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
  • Exposure to platforms such as Amazon Connect or similar customer engagement systems.

Desirable
  • Understanding of government operating environments.
  • Knowledge of customer experience, service delivery and operational performance reporting.
  • Understanding of basic project management principles.
  • Experience working with large-scale operational datasets.

Benefits
  • Contract opportunity through to 30 June 2027 with Potential Extension
  • $61.86 per hour plus Superannuation
  • Opportunities available across multiple Australian locations: Dandenong, VIC; Richmond, VIC; Geelong, VIC; Footscray, VIC; Deakin, ACT; Midland, WA; Robina, QLD
  • Work within a collaborative analytics and reporting team.
  • Contribute to meaningful customer and service delivery outcomes.
Eligibility Australian Citizenship is mandatory for this opportunity.

If you have a passion for data, reporting, performance analytics and driving business improvement through insights, we encourage you to APPLY NOW.

Applications close: Friday 13 November 2026.

job.title: Lead Release & Platform Engineer
job.description:
We're seeking a Lead Release & Platform Engineer to drive release engineering, deployment integrity, and platform alignment across a large-scale transformation program.
This is a high-impact role where you'll lead release strategy, code management practices, and cross-platform delivery across a complex ecosystem of SaaS, cloud, digital, integration, and data platforms. This is a 12-month contract role with our client AGL, based in Melbourne CBD, in a hybrid working environment.

What You'll Do
  • Own release engineering and code management standards across multiple platforms.
  • Lead branching, merging, versioning, release governance, and deployment practices.
  • Drive CI/CD, release automation, environment promotion, and rollback readiness.
  • Coordinate major releases across engineering teams, vendors, and technology platforms.
  • Ensure end-to-end platform compatibility, release readiness, and technical risk management.
  • Provide clear engineering insights and recommendations to delivery and leadership teams.

About You
You are a senior engineering professional with extensive experience in Release Engineering, DevOps, Platform Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, or Software Engineering within large and complex technology environments.

You'll Bring:
  • Strong experience leading release and deployment practices across multiple engineering teams.
  • Advanced Git/GitHub expertise, including branching strategies, merge management, pull request controls, tagging, and release traceability.
  • Deep knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, artifact management, feature flags, configuration management, environment promotion, and rollback strategies.
  • Experience delivering integrated releases involving SaaS platforms, custom-built applications, APIs, cloud services, and vendor-managed solutions.
  • Strong understanding of release governance, operational readiness, change control, security requirements, and production support.
  • The ability to communicate technical risks and recommendations to both engineering and executive stakeholders.
  • Proven experience influencing teams, driving accountability, and establishing engineering standards.

If you're passionate about release engineering, platform reliability, and delivering change at scale, we'd love to hear from you. Please click APPLY NOW and follow the prompts.

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle

  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:

  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:

  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:

  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the operation and isn't afraid to make decisions.

You'll be taking over an established operation with experienced people and established ways of working.

The opportunity is to build on what's working, identify what can be improved and lead the team through positive change.

We're looking for someone who:

  • Takes ownership
  • Leads from the front
  • Makes decisions
  • Holds people accountable
  • Develops and supports their team
  • Builds strong customer relationships
  • Looks for better ways of doing things
  • Can balance people, customers and commercial outcomes
What's on Offer

  • $165,000 – $175,000 + super
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • STI / incentive program
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
  • Staff discounts and additional benefits
  • Opportunity to lead a substantial operation within an established national business
  • Genuine scope to influence operational performance and branch growth
Apply Now

If you're an experienced Branch or Operations Manager looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership and make a measurable impact, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated resume and cover letter.

Early applications are encouraged, as shortlisting may commence before the closing date of Friday 2 October 2026.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated confidentially.

job.title: Senior Case Manager (Administrative Review Tribunal)
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Case Manager to manage a portfolio of complex review matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
This role requires a highly organised professional who can exercise sound judgement, navigate complex issues, and build strong stakeholder relationships. You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of cases, identifying resolution pathways, gathering and analysing information, and contributing to positive outcomes through effective case management and dispute resolution practices.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Manage end-to-end case management activities for matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
  • Analyse complex information and develop options to support early and effective resolution.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Obtain, assess, and interpret evidence to support decision-making and case outcomes.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, correspondence, reports, and case management documentation.
  • Attend and participate in Case Conferences, Conciliations, and Hearings.
  • Apply negotiation, advocacy, and dispute resolution techniques to resolve matters efficiently.
  • Identify, assess, and respond to risks impacting participants, operational outcomes, and business objectives.
  • Manage competing priorities and meet legislated and operational timeframes.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and best-practice case management approaches.


You Must Have
 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, sensitive, or high-risk cases.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective working relationships.
  • Proven analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to make sound decisions.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing detailed reports, briefs, or recommendations.
  • Strong verbal communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume and deadline-driven environment.
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, or procedural frameworks.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to exercise professional judgement in complex situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team while managing an independent caseload
  • Experience with administrative law, merits review, tribunal, or appeals processes.
  • Experience within disability, health, community services, government, or social services environments.
  • Experience in insurance claims, underwriting, actuarial services, or compensation schemes.
  • Experience in dispute resolution, investigations, complaints handling, or regulatory case management.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Melbourne, VIC
  • $60.26 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.title: Internal Review Officer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Internal Review Officer to undertake reviews of decisions relating to participant access, eligibility, and funded supports.
This role is suited to professionals who enjoy analysing complex information, interpreting legislation and policy, and making evidence-based recommendations. You will manage a caseload of review matters while ensuring decisions are completed accurately, within required timeframes, and in line with legislative and operational requirements.
The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical skills, attention to detail, sound judgement, and a commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Undertake internal reviews by gathering, assessing, and analysing information and evidence.
  • Apply relevant legislation, policy, operational guidelines, and procedures to support fair and consistent recommendations.
  • Prepare clear, objective, and well-reasoned review findings and recommendations.
  • Communicate review outcomes, review rights, and appeal pathways in a professional and timely manner.
  • Engage with participants, representatives, and stakeholders to obtain information and support informed decision-making.
  • Manage a caseload of review matters while meeting legislative and operational timeframes.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation to support compliant and defensible review processes.
  • Apply person-centred, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive approaches when dealing with sensitive matters.
  • Contribute to quality assurance activities, continuous improvement initiatives, and service delivery enhancements.
  • Maintain knowledge of relevant legislation, policy, and operational frameworks.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, procedures, or regulatory frameworks.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyse information and evidence to develop logical, balanced, and defensible recommendations.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to make sound decisions based on available information.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, findings, recommendations, or assessments.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and caseloads within established timeframes.
  • Ability to manage sensitive or complex matters using sound judgement and professionalism.
  • Strong organisational skills and experience maintaining accurate records and case documentation.
  • Commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes and high-quality customer service.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment while managing individual responsibilities.

Highly Desirable
  • Experience within government, administrative review, regulatory, disability, health, community services, or human services environments.
  • Knowledge of administrative review processes and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Experience assessing complex information and preparing recommendations in a legislative or policy-driven environment.
  • Knowledge of disability, functional impact, or participant-centred service delivery models.
  • Experience using case management, customer relationship management (CRM), or workflow management systems.
  • Qualifications in Law, Public Administration, Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Disability Studies, or a related discipline.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Melbourne, VIC
  • $55.24 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.



Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.title: Contracting Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Contracting Officer to support the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.
You will join a fast-paced, high-profile environment where your procurement and contracting expertise will directly support complex, strategically significant outcomes across the nuclear-powered submarine program.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the APS6 Contracting Officer is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing specialist procurement and contracting advice and end-to-end support across procurement planning, market approaches, contract establishment and contract management.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will strengthen Australia’s national security and deliver lasting economic and industrial benefits for generations to come.
In this role, you will manage complex procurement and contract management activities while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, policies and the Commonwealth procurement framework. You will provide practical, risk-informed commercial advice and develop solutions to complex procurement challenges.

About the Team
The Commercial Branch delivers end-to-end procurement, contracting and commercial support across the Australian Submarine Agency, enabling the successful delivery of Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine program.
You will join a professional and collaborative team that values innovation, integrity and continuous improvement, and works closely with stakeholders across the Agency to deliver compliant, value-for-money, strategically aligned procurement outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering procurement and contracting outcomes, including:
  • Providing specialist procurement and contracting advice to support complex, strategically significant outcomes
  • Supporting procurement planning and commercial strategy development
  • Drafting approaches to market, supporting evaluations, and contributing to negotiations through to contract execution
  • Managing contract formation and ongoing contract management activities
  • Reviewing contract change proposals and commercial deliverables, and advising on performance outcomes
  • Identifying, assessing and advising on commercial risks and contractual matters
  • Providing practical, policy-aligned advice across procurement legislation, frameworks and best practice
  • Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal stakeholders, and engaging with legal and finance advisers as required
  • Supporting capability uplift and continuous improvement across procurement/commercial practices
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Experience managing complex procurements end-to-end (strategy, approach to market, evaluation, negotiation, contract execution)
  • Experience providing commercial support across contract management (performance, change, remediation)
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and sound judgement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to tailor advice for different audiences
  • Ability to work strategically in a sensitive, fast-paced environment with competing priorities
  • Proven ability to build and sustain effective stakeholder relationships
  • Adaptability, resilience and flexibility in a changing environment
  • Sound understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Framework
Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.

Location / Work Arrangement
  • Locations may include: Canberra ACT, Melbourne VIC, Port Adelaide SA, Rockingham WA
  • On-site work arrangements apply, with flexibility considered in line with operational and business requirements

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines,  to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

job.title: Contracting Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Contracting Officer to support the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.
You will join a fast-paced, high-profile environment where your procurement and contracting expertise will directly support complex, strategically significant outcomes across the nuclear-powered submarine program.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the APS6 Contracting Officer is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing specialist procurement and contracting advice and end-to-end support across procurement planning, market approaches, contract establishment and contract management.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will strengthen Australia’s national security and deliver lasting economic and industrial benefits for generations to come.
In this role, you will manage complex procurement and contract management activities while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, policies and the Commonwealth procurement framework. You will provide practical, risk-informed commercial advice and develop solutions to complex procurement challenges.

About the Team
The Commercial Branch delivers end-to-end procurement, contracting and commercial support across the Australian Submarine Agency, enabling the successful delivery of Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine program.
You will join a professional and collaborative team that values innovation, integrity and continuous improvement, and works closely with stakeholders across the Agency to deliver compliant, value-for-money, strategically aligned procurement outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering procurement and contracting outcomes, including:
  • Providing specialist procurement and contracting advice to support complex, strategically significant outcomes
  • Supporting procurement planning and commercial strategy development
  • Drafting approaches to market, supporting evaluations, and contributing to negotiations through to contract execution
  • Managing contract formation and ongoing contract management activities
  • Reviewing contract change proposals and commercial deliverables, and advising on performance outcomes
  • Identifying, assessing and advising on commercial risks and contractual matters
  • Providing practical, policy-aligned advice across procurement legislation, frameworks and best practice
  • Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal stakeholders, and engaging with legal and finance advisers as required
  • Supporting capability uplift and continuous improvement across procurement/commercial practices
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Experience managing complex procurements end-to-end (strategy, approach to market, evaluation, negotiation, contract execution)
  • Experience providing commercial support across contract management (performance, change, remediation)
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and sound judgement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to tailor advice for different audiences
  • Ability to work strategically in a sensitive, fast-paced environment with competing priorities
  • Proven ability to build and sustain effective stakeholder relationships
  • Adaptability, resilience and flexibility in a changing environment
  • Sound understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Framework
Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.

Location / Work Arrangement
  • Locations may include: Canberra ACT, Melbourne VIC, Port Adelaide SA, Rockingham WA
  • On-site work arrangements apply, with flexibility considered in line with operational and business requirements
Apply Now
If you are an experienced procurement and contracting professional seeking to contribute to a once-in-a-lifetime national program, we encourage you to apply today.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Finance Business Partner to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within the ASA environment, the APS6 Finance Business Partner is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing strategic financial analysis, assurance and advice to support the delivery of budgets and outcomes, including across the capability development process.

The acquisition of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.
Within the ASA Finance Branch, you will support agency and program-wide decision-making through the development and implementation of processes that enable accurate, timely financial information and insight in a complex, fast-paced, high-profile environment.

About the Team
The ASA Finance Branch supports the Chief Financial Officer, the Assistant Director General Program Costing, and the broader ASA through the provision of expert strategic support and advice relating to the acquisition, sustainment and disposal of nuclear-powered submarines (NPS).
ASA fosters an inclusive culture that emphasises respect and collaboration and prioritises safety and security. You will be working at the cutting edge of capability delivery, supported by professionalisation pathways and unique career opportunities.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering finance business partnering outcomes, including:
  • Providing strategic financial analysis, assurance and advice to support budgets, outcomes and capability delivery
  • Developing and maintaining collaborative finance business partnerships, including identifying financial risks and opportunities
  • Supporting business leads with budget proposals and performance reviews, including assessing contracts/agreements for financial impacts against schedule
  • Contributing to financial aspects of asset management (e.g., asset reconciliations, Asset Valuation Models (AVMs), Project Capitalisation Plans, asset rollouts, aged/uncleared balances)
  • Preparing high-quality briefs and reports that identify issues and provide practical recommendations
  • Working within relevant Commonwealth financial and budgeting frameworks, legislation, policy and processes
  • Managing competing priorities while exercising initiative and judgement to achieve outcomes
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Proven experience providing strategic financial advice and analysis in complex stakeholder environments
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills (you can partner effectively with senior stakeholders)
  • Sound understanding of commercial cost drivers and the financial impacts on deliverables
  • Experience preparing briefs, reports and recommendations to support decision-making
  • Ability to work independently with autonomy, initiative and accountability in a high-paced environment
Mandatory qualifications / experience (required)
Relevant experience as a Finance Business Partner / Finance Adviser (APS6 level or equivalent), ideally within government or similarly complex environments.

Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.
Flexible working arrangements may be supported where aligned with operational and business requirements.

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines,  to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Driver - Light Rigid
job.description:
Light Rigid Driver & Canine Attendant (Casual)

Location: Bulla
Employment Type: Casual
Availability: Min 3 days availability

Are you an experienced Light Rigid Driver who loves working with dogs? We are seeking a reliable, physically fit and motivated individual to join our team supporting a highly specialised canine program.

This unique role combines driving responsibilities with hands-on canine care, providing an opportunity to work with a professional team dedicated to the health, welfare and development of working dogs.
Key Responsibilities
  • Drive Light Rigid vehicles with both automatic and manual transmissions
  • Clean, feed, groom and exercise a colony of canines
  • Monitor canine health and welfare
  • Conduct routine health and welfare checks
  • Administer medication under veterinary direction
  • Issue food, equipment and supplies appropriate to each canine's age and development stage
  • Facilitate the safe transport of canines and equipment across Melbourne and Greater Geelong
  • Accompany canines to veterinary and specialist appointments
  • Maintain fleet vehicles and ensure they are clean, safe and roadworthy
  • Interact professionally with internal and external stakeholders
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation
  • Clean and maintain facilities, vehicles and equipment in accordance with operational guidelines
About You
  • Hold a current Light Rigid (LR) Licence
  • Confident driving both manual and automatic vehicles
  • Experience in canine care, animal handling, animal husbandry or a related field is highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
  • Physically fit and able to meet basic mobility and fitness requirements
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Able to work independently and collaboratively within a team
  • Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
  • Capable of managing competing priorities and changing schedules
  • Committed to following operational procedures, safety requirements and animal welfare standards at all times
  • Pass full security clearances incl
What's on Offer
  • Casual role offering 3-4 days per week
  • Variety in your day with a mix of driving and animal care duties
  • Work alongside experienced canine, veterinary and operational teams
  • Opportunity to contribute to the care and development of highly trained working dogs
  • Supportive team environment
If you're passionate about animal welfare, enjoy driving, and are looking for a rewarding role where no two days are the same, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today!

job.title: Plant Operator
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking a motivated and reliable Plant Operator to support the operation team at Baiada Rendering Plant, Tamworth.
This is a fantastic opportunity to secure ongoing work with competitive pay rates, penalties and allowances, while building a long-term career with one of Australia's largest poultry producers.
 
  • Competitive hourly rates plus shift penalties and allowances
  • Monday - Saturday | 7am - 11pm
  • Potential for permanency following probation

About the Role
As a Plant Operator, you will play a key role in the safe and efficient operation of the rendering facility. You will be responsible for monitoring production processes, operating plant equipment, conducting routine checks, and maintaining high standards of safety, quality, and hygiene.
This is a hands-on position that requires physical fitness, attention to detail, and a strong commitment to workplace safety.

Key Responsibilities
  • Operate and monitor rendering plant equipment and processes
  • Conduct routine plant inspections and operational checks
  • Load and unload vehicles and materials as required
  • Complete production, monitoring, and quality records accurately
  • Assist with troubleshooting and reporting plant issues
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organised work environment
  • Perform general cleaning duties including hosing, washing down equipment, sweeping, foaming, sanitising, and using water guns and hand tools
  • Follow all site biosecurity, safety, quality, and environmental procedures
  • Assist with the handling and movement of finished product and by-products
Comprehensive training will be provided to successful candidates.

About You
We are looking for dependable individuals who enjoy hands-on work and thrive in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Essential Requirements
  • Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident
  • Current driver's licence and reliable transport
  • Strong commitment to safety and workplace procedures
  • Physically fit and capable of repetitive manual handling
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment involving heat, noise, odours, and wet conditions
  • Good communication skills and attention to detail
  • Basic computer skills for recording operational data
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Reliable, punctual, and willing to learn
Desirable Skills & Experience
  • Previous experience in manufacturing, production, processing, rendering, waste management, or similar industrial environments
  • Forklift licence and operating experience
  • Mechanical aptitude or experience operating machinery
  • Experience performing plant checks and monitoring production processes
  • Understanding of workplace safety and quality systems
About Baiada
Baiada Poultry is one of Australia's leading poultry producers, supplying trusted brands Steggles and Lilydale Free Range to Australian families for over 100 years. With a fully integrated operation from farm to table, Baiada is committed to delivering high-quality poultry products while maintaining strong standards in safety, quality, animal welfare, and sustainability.

How to Apply
Click APPLY or contact the Baiada Team on 02 6762 9000 and baiadatamworth@chandlermacleod.com for a confidential discussion. job.title: Dock hand
job.description:
Dock Hand | Upper Coomera | $38.61 per Hour
Are you an experienced Dock Hand looking for your next opportunity with a leading national freight and logistics operation? We are currently seeking reliable, safety-focused and hardworking individuals to join a busy transport and distribution team based in Upper Coomera.
This is a fast-paced role suited to candidates who enjoy physical work, can work efficiently in a team environment, and are committed to maintaining high safety standards.

What's on Offer?
  • Competitive pay rates of $38.61
  • Ongoing casual opportunities with potential for long-term work
  • Immediate starts available
  • Supportive team environment
  • Day and Afternoon shifts available
Available Shift Times
  • 10:00am - 6:30pm (30-minute unpaid break)
  • 1:30pm - 10:00pm (30-minute unpaid break)
Key Responsibilities
  • Loading and unloading freight from trailers and dock areas
  • Sorting and staging freight for dispatch
  • Manual handling of parcels and general freight
  • Pick packing and freight preparation duties
  • Maintaining a clean and safe work environment
  • Following workplace health and safety procedures at all times
Essential Criteria
  • Previous dock hand, freight handling, warehouse or logistics experience
  • Pick packing experience
  • Strong commitment to workplace safety
  • Reliable with excellent attendance and punctuality
  • Physically fit and capable of repetitive manual handling

If you're looking for a rewarding opportunity, click APPLY NOW and submit your application today.
