job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines, at APS 6, Executive Level 1 and Executive Level 2, to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
  • At EL1 and EL2, leading teams, planning and managing technical programs and resources, and mentoring developing engineers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
  • For EL1 and EL2 roles, demonstrated leadership, supervision and mentoring experience
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

This is a unique chance for an experienced EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations will lead a critical function within the Infrastructure Planning, Performance and Integration (IPPI) team, supporting the delivery of a complex, nationally significant infrastructure portfolio.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.
The ASA’s Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division is responsible for planning and coordinating the delivery of physical infrastructure that will:
  • Enable AUKUS partners to have a rotational presence at HMAS Stirling
  • Support Australia’s acquisition and sustainment of Virginia Class submarines
  • Deliver Australia’s sovereign build and sustainment of SSN-AUKUS submarines
In this role, you will use commercial, workforce, financial and business operations levers to improve organisational performance, strengthen delivery confidence and enable informed executive decision-making.
This position is eligible for an additional remuneration benefit known within ASA as a Building Capability Payment (BCP), applied in addition to base salary for critical capability disciplines.

About the Team
The Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division coordinates the infrastructure that enables Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine capability. The work spans major programs and sites across Western Australia and South Australia, bringing together government, industry and international partners to deliver nationally significant outcomes.
You’ll join a collaborative, high-performing environment where you can shape strategy, influence delivery outcomes and contribute to one of Australia’s most complex infrastructure portfolios.

Key Responsibilities: 
You will be responsible for leading and enabling infrastructure operations outcomes, including:
  • Leading and growing high-performing teams, building capability and fostering a culture of accountability and collaboration
  • Driving continuous improvement across reporting, governance, information management and organisational performance
  • Providing strategic leadership and sound judgement to solve complex problems and balance competing priorities
  • Strengthening delivery confidence through robust performance oversight, insights and operational levers
  • Applying strong commercial, financial and business management acumen to translate data into decisions and action
  • Influencing outcomes across diverse stakeholder groups where success relies on collaboration rather than direct authority
  • Identifying and managing enterprise risks, opportunities and dependencies to improve delivery outcomes
  • Operating effectively in ambiguity, providing clear advice and direction in evolving environments
  • Preparing and delivering high-quality advice and communication to senior executives, government stakeholders and delivery partners
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Proven leadership experience in complex operational, portfolio, program or infrastructure environments
  • Strong commercial, financial and business management capability
  • Experience improving organisational performance through governance, reporting and insight-led decision-making
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines | APS 6, EL1 & EL2
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines, at APS 6, Executive Level 1 and Executive Level 2, to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
  • At EL1 and EL2, leading teams, planning and managing technical programs and resources, and mentoring developing engineers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
  • For EL1 and EL2 roles, demonstrated leadership, supervision and mentoring experience
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now

Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

job.title: Planner
job.description:
Planner – Participant Safeguarding Advisory Team
  • Canberra, Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney or Hobart
  • $61.86 per hour plus super
  • January start date until 31 December 2027 – with potential to extend
     

The why.
We are recruiting experienced Planners to join a national Safeguarding Advisory Team focused on supporting people with disability through specialised safeguarding advice, risk assessment and intervention support.
This is a rewarding opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes for participants by providing expert advice, managing complex safeguarding matters and supporting frontline staff in navigating sensitive and high-risk situations.


What’s in it for you?
  • Potential career progression within this high-profile federal government agency
  • Fast paced and dynamic environment
  • Great onboarding experience with a diverse and inclusive team culture.
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangement
  • Weekly pay cycle
  • $61.86 per hour
  • January start date until 31 December 2027 – with potential to extend

The company.
As a Planner within the Safeguarding Advisory Team, you will be responsible for assessing complex participant circumstances, identifying risks, and providing specialised safeguarding advice to support positive participant outcomes.
Working within a collaborative national team, you will partner with internal stakeholders and external agencies to coordinate safeguarding activities, deliver interventions, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen safeguarding practices across the organisation

The responsibility.
  • Undertake risk identification and assessment of complex and sensitive participant situations.
  • Provide specialised written and verbal safeguarding advice to staff managing high-risk matters.
  • Facilitate discussions and support decision-making in relation to safeguarding concerns.
  • Work directly with participants requiring urgent and short-term safeguarding interventions.
  • Liaise with external agencies and authorities to coordinate appropriate safeguarding responses.
  • Coach and mentor colleagues while contributing to knowledge sharing and capability uplift.
  • Assist with quality improvement initiatives, process enhancements and service delivery outcomes.
  • Manage competing priorities while maintaining accurate documentation and records.

About you.
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Experience working with complex case management, safeguarding, risk, disability, health, human services or social support environments.
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to assess complex situations and make informed decisions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear and practical advice.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to manage sensitive conversations.
  • Experience interpreting legislation, policies and procedures in a professional environment.
  • Ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team environment.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Desirable knowledge and experience
  • Knowledge of the disability services legislative and operating environment, including participant safeguarding principles and risk management practices.
  • Experience with planning processes, CRM systems or other relevant operational business systems.
  • Experience contributing to operational guidance, procedures, frameworks or training materials.



The essentials.
•         Baseline Security Clearance (AGSVA), or ability to obtain.
•        NDIS Worker Screening Check, or ability to obtain.
•        Australian Citizenship

The next steps.

If you are interested in this role, please APPLY NOW by submitting your resume in MS Word Format as shortlisting may commence early.

Customer Service | Hire Operations | Equipment & Yard Support

Chandler Macleod is seeking a reliable and hands-on Hire Assistant to join a busy equipment hire business based in Fairfield.

This is a varied role suited to someone who enjoys customer interaction, working in a fast-paced environment and being involved in both administrative and practical tasks.

You'll split your time between the hire office, yard and deliveries, supporting daily branch operations and ensuring customers receive the right equipment, on time and in the right condition.

Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Previous experience in equipment hire, trade services, construction, customer service or a similar environment
  • Strong customer service and communication skills

  • A hands-on attitude and willingness to assist with yard operations
  • Good organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • Strong attention to detail and a safety-focused approach
  • The ability to work independently and take initiative

Qualifications & Training
The following qualifications are highly regarded:
  • Forklift Licence
  • First Aid Certificate
  • Test and Tag Certification

Don't hold all the above qualifications? No problem! The business is willing to sponsor successful candidates to obtain the required qualifications and certifications.

What's on Offer?
  • Salary: $78,000 + superannuation
  • Location: Fairfield, VIC
  • Employment: Full-time
  • Employer-sponsored training and certifications where required
  • A varied role combining office duties, customer interaction and hands-on work
  • Exposure to different aspects of equipment hire and branch operations

Working Hours
  • Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday & Friday: 6:45am – 5:15pm

Additional hours may be required depending on operational needs.

job.title: Mechanical Enginneer
job.description:
MECHANICAL ENGINEER
Electric & Mechanical Drive Mining Trucks
Rutherford | Permanent, Full-Time

• Contribute to the development of heavy mining trucks.
• Follow your work from mechanical design through to testing and field improvements.
• Use your English and Mandarin skills in an international engineering environment.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
Chandler Macleod is seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a growing mining equipment business based in Rutherford, in the Newcastle/Hunter region.

This is an opportunity to work on electric and mechanical drive off-highway mining trucks, helping turn engineering designs into practical solutions for demanding operating environments.
Working alongside experienced engineers and colleagues in China, you’ll contribute across the equipment lifecycle—from design and development through to prototype builds, commissioning, testing and ongoing improvements.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
• Develop mechanical designs across chassis, suspension, drivetrain, cooling systems and structural assemblies.
• Produce 3D models, engineering drawings, specifications and bills of materials.
• Carry out engineering calculations and support structural, fatigue and thermal analysis.
• Assist with prototype builds, inspections, commissioning and field testing.
• Investigate technical issues and improve equipment reliability, safety and serviceability.
• Collaborate with electrical, hydraulic, manufacturing, service and supplier teams.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING
• You’ll hold a qualification in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline, with practical engineering experience and confidence using 3D CAD software.
• Experience in heavy equipment, mining, automotive or industrial manufacturing will be highly regarded. You’ll also bring sound mechanical design knowledge, practical problem-solving skills and a collaborative approach
• Fluency in English and Mandarin is essential, as the role involves regular technical collaboration with engineering colleagues in China.
• Project management and commercial tender experience would be an advantage.

WHY CONSIDER THIS ROLE?
This position offers varied, hands-on engineering work with large mining equipment. You’ll have the opportunity to see how your designs perform in practice, contribute to equipment improvements and develop your capability alongside experienced engineers.

INTERESTED?
Apply with your current CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant engineering experience and Mandarin proficiency.

For a confidential discussion, contact:
Mark Seery | Senior Recruitment Consultant
Chandler Macleod
0437 356 484

job.title: Internal Sales & Account Management
job.description:
We are seeking a commercially minded and personable Internal Sales & Account Management to join an established plant and equipment hire business based in Dandenong South.

A large part of your day will involve proactively contacting existing and previous clients, keeping the business front of mind and understanding their upcoming projects and equipment requirements. You'll also manage inbound hire enquiries, prepare and follow up quotes, re-engage dormant clients and identify opportunities to develop new business.

There is a genuine sales element to the role, so you'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, starting conversations and asking for the business. However, this isn't a traditional BDM position focused solely on cold acquisition or being out on the road.

Working within a small, close-knit team, you'll also be someone who is happy to jump in and assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries when needed.


Key Responsibilities
  • Proactively contact existing, previous and prospective clients to generate hire opportunities
  • Build and maintain relationships with clients across the civil and construction sectors
  • Re-engage dormant clients and identify upcoming projects or equipment requirements
  • Manage inbound hire enquiries via phone and email
  • Prepare quotes and proactively follow up outstanding opportunities
  • Identify and approach prospective clients where appropriate
  • Promote available equipment to maximise fleet utilisation
  • Maintain accurate client and sales activity within HubSpot CRM
  • Assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries across the office when required
  • Conduct phone and Microsoft Teams meetings, with occasional site visits where beneficial
  • Work closely with the wider team to maintain client engagement and sales momentum

About You
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys speaking with clients and is comfortable with the commercial side of relationship building.

You'll ideally be:
  • Confident making proactive outbound calls and asking clients about upcoming requirements
  • Personable, genuine and able to build rapport quickly
  • Commercially minded and comfortable identifying sales opportunities
  • Comfortable approaching new clients as well as working with established relationships
  • Persistent with follow-ups without being overly pushy
  • Reliable, consistent and willing to get involved wherever needed
  • Organised and disciplined with quotes, follow-ups and CRM activity
  • Comfortable working autonomously within a small office environment
  • Looking for a stable, long-term opportunity where you can become a valued part of the team

Experience within plant and equipment hire, earthmoving, civil construction, construction or a related industry will be highly regarded. Strong internal sales, hire or client relationship experience from another industry will also be considered.


What's on Offer
  • $80,000–$85,000 + super
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Dandenong South location
  • 100% office-based, with occasional site visits
  • Small, close-knit and down-to-earth team
  • Established client relationships to build upon
  • A varied mix of client relationships, hire coordination and proactive sales
  • Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business

job.title: FP&A Manager
job.description:
Commercial FP&A Manager, ANZ | Growing Biotech

This is a fast-growing biotech business in the middle of a global expansion. They need a finance partner who sits inside the commercial engine, not behind it. You’ll work directly with the ANZ leadership and sales teams, own the full FP&A cycle, and use it to shape how the business grows, prices and invests.

A big part of the role is working hand in hand with sales. You’ll get to know the seasonal patterns that drive demand, understand what’s behind the peaks and troughs, and turn that into forecasts the business can plan around. As the company scales into new markets, getting this right matters more every quarter.

This is a lean, growing business, so your work is visible and your input counts. Leadership will come to you when they need to understand the numbers and decide what to do next. That takes clear insight, practical forecasting and the confidence to push back when something doesn’t stack up.

What you’ll be doing

  • Partner with senior leaders and the sales team on performance and growth
  • Work closely with sales to understand seasonal cycles and build them into accurate, practical forecasts
  • Own budgeting, forecasting and monthly performance reporting across ANZ
  • Explain revenue, margin, cost and working capital results in plain commercial terms
  • Build scenario models to support pricing, investment and expansion decisions
  • Build and improve forecasting models and reporting from the ground up, using Xero and Excel
  • Find smarter ways to automate reporting and give leadership better visibility as the business scales
What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in finance, with strong FP&A experience
  • Hands-on business partnering with sales or commercial teams
  • Experience forecasting in a business with seasonal or cyclical demand (highly regarded)
  • Advanced Excel and strong modelling skills, with Power BI or similar a plus
  • Experience with Xero or similar cloud accounting platforms
  • A hands-on approach and comfort building things without a big team or established systems around you
  • The confidence to influence senior leaders and work through ambiguity

job.title: Asset Manager
job.description:
Role Overview:
We are seeking an Asset Manager to take ownership of the performance, reliability, risk profile and long-term lifecycle management of a portfolio of critical energy infrastructure assets located across Victoria, New South Wales and potentially New Zealand.
A key focus of the role will be supporting assets such as synchronous condensers and terminal stations, ensuring they continue to operate safely, efficiently and in line with operational and business objectives.
Success in this position will come from combining strong technical capability with effective stakeholder engagement, commercial awareness and a proactive approach to continuous improvement. Just as important as technical experience is a willingness to learn, accept feedback and contribute positively to the wider team.

The Opportunity:
This role will play a key part in optimising the performance and reliability of strategically important electrical infrastructure assets.
Working alongside engineering, maintenance, operations and commercial teams, you will support the development of asset strategies, oversee risk management activities, improve asset performance and help guide long-term investment decisions.
The position provides a balance of office-based work, stakeholder engagement and occasional site travel, offering exposure to both the technical and commercial aspects of asset ownership.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Drive asset performance, reliability and lifecycle outcomes across a portfolio of electrical infrastructure assets.
  • Assist in developing and implementing asset management plans and strategies.
  • Monitor asset condition, risk, performance and compliance requirements.
  • Identify and support opportunities to improve asset performance and efficiency.
  • Contribute to capital planning, budgeting and investment decisions.
  • Work collaboratively with operational, engineering and maintenance teams.
  • Support the management and mitigation of technical and commercial risks.
  • Coordinate and engage with external contractors and service providers.
  • Participate in periodic site visits across Victoria and New South Wales.
  • Contribute to the ongoing reliability and sustainability of the asset portfolio.
Skills & Experience Essential:
  • Experience within Asset Management, Asset Engineering, Reliability Engineering or Asset Performance environments.
  • Understanding of asset lifecycle and maintenance management principles.
  • Exposure to electrical, utility or infrastructure-based assets.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Knowledge of risk management and reliability methodologies.
  • Ability to evaluate both technical and commercial considerations.
  • Well-developed organisational and prioritisation skills.
Desirable:
  • Experience working with or around Synchronous Condensers.
  • Exposure to Terminal Station or Substation assets.
  • Transmission, power systems or broader electrical infrastructure experience.
  • Utilities, renewable energy or critical infrastructure background.
  • Exposure to HV assets and electrical networks.
  • Experience contributing to asset strategy, maintenance optimisation or investment planning activities.
About You: We're looking for someone who brings strong technical foundations, but equally demonstrates the attitude and mindset required to grow within the role.
You will ideally be someone who:
  • Takes initiative and ownership of their work.
  • Has a genuine desire to learn and develop.
  • Welcomes feedback and uses it constructively.
  • Isn't afraid to ask questions when faced with unfamiliar challenges.
  • Has a strong interest in asset performance and infrastructure reliability.
  • Is organised, accountable and dependable.
  • Can adapt to changing priorities and challenges.
  • Builds positive relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • Is motivated by making assets perform better, rather than simply chasing a title.
Importantly, this opportunity is open to candidates who may be stepping into a larger Asset Management role. The focus is less on finding the most senior person and more on finding someone with the right technical foundation, attitude, growth mindset and willingness to get stuck in and develop.

Working Arrangements:
  • Permanent full-time opportunity.
  • Hybrid model with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely.
  • Initial onboarding period will be office-based.
  • Approximately 1-2 site visits per month.
  • Travel across Victoria and New South Wales as required.
  • Potential future travel to New Zealand.

job.title: Senior Commissioning Engineer
job.description:
Senior Commissioning Engineer Permanent Role | Major HV & Power Infrastructure Projects | Melbourne / VIC

A leading Australian power and energy infrastructure organisation is seeking an experienced Senior Commissioning Engineer to join their team.

This role is ideally suited to a commissioning professional with strong experience operating within regulated electricity network environments and a background in testing, commissioning, protection systems, energisation and utility infrastructure.
Working across projects up to 500kV, you will take ownership of commissioning activities from planning and testing through to energisation and final handover.

The Opportunity: You will play a key role in the delivery of critical electrical infrastructure, supporting large-scale transmission, distribution, renewable energy, data centre and network infrastructure projects.
The successful candidate will be responsible for the testing, commissioning and energisation of primary and secondary systems while ensuring compliance with utility standards, safety requirements and operational frameworks.

Key Responsibilities:
Testing & Commissioning (Senior Level)
  • Lead HV testing and commissioning activities on primary plant from 415V through to 500kV.
  • Perform secondary injection testing across a broad range of protection schemes.
  • Test protection relays, control systems, SCADA and communications platforms.
  • Integrate AC and DC control systems in both greenfield and brownfield environments.
  • Review designs and drawings to validate protection schemes and constructability.
  • Apply, verify and modify IED settings using OEM software.
  • Develop commissioning methodologies, test plans, ITPs and acceptance documentation.
  • Support energisation programs, outage activities and operational handovers.
Highly Regarded Qualifications:

Candidates holding any of the following will be viewed favourably:
  • Advanced Diploma of ESI (Power Systems)
  • Electrical Engineering Degree
  • Protection & Control qualifications
  • HV Switching Authorisations
  • Senior Authorised Person experience
  • Utility competency programs
  • Network access competencies
  • Utility-specific authorisations and approvals
Candidates holding an Advanced Diploma of ESI (Power Systems), HV Switching Authorisations, utility network competencies or previous experience working within regulated network environments are strongly encouraged to apply.

Utility & Network Experience:

Candidates with experience operating within regulated electricity network environments are strongly encouraged to apply.
We are particularly interested in professionals who can demonstrate:
  • Experience working within transmission, distribution or utility network environments.
  • Exposure to utility operating standards, procedures and approval frameworks.
  • Experience supporting testing, commissioning and energisation activities on live network assets.
  • HV switching, outage coordination and operational access experience.
  • Previous involvement in transmission, distribution and substation infrastructure projects.
  • Experience operating under network authorisations, permits and access requirements.
  • Participation in network energisation programs and staged commissioning activities.
Experience working alongside electricity network operators, utility asset owners and network service providers will be highly regarded.

Desired Experience:
Transmission & Distribution Infrastructure
  • Transmission substations
  • Distribution substations
  • Terminal stations
  • Zone substations
  • Utility infrastructure projects
  • Network augmentation projects
Critical Infrastructure
  • Data Centres
  • Renewable Energy Projects
  • Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS)
  • Generation Assets
  • Rail & Traction Infrastructure
Protection & Control Systems Experience working with:
  • SEL
  • Siemens Siprotec
  • ABB Relion
  • GE Multilin
  • MiCOM / Areva
Testing Equipment Experience using:
  • Omicron Test Universe
  • CMC256 / CMC356
  • CPC100
  • CT Analyser
  • Doble Protection Suite
  • Secondary and primary injection testing equipment
About You:

Qualifications & Experience
  • Degree qualified in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years' experience in testing and commissioning of primary and secondary systems.
  • Strong understanding of power system protection principles and applications.
  • Proven experience leading commissioning activities within utility, industrial or infrastructure environments.
  • IEC 61850 exposure highly regarded.
  • Strong understanding of testing, commissioning and energisation principles.
Leadership & Project Delivery:
  • Lead and coordinate commissioning teams, subcontractors and technical specialists.
  • Develop commissioning strategies that improve safety, efficiency and project outcomes.
  • Manage commissioning schedules, outage coordination and staged implementation activities.
  • Provide senior technical support to project managers, designers and site teams.
  • Mentor and support commissioning engineers, technicians and electricians.
  • Act as a key technical stakeholder during testing, commissioning and energisation phases.
Safety & Stakeholder Engagement:
  • Drive a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with WHS requirements.
  • Identify, manage and mitigate commissioning and energisation risks.
  • Work closely with clients, senior management and external stakeholders.
  • Provide clear reporting on commissioning progress, risks and outcomes.
  • Ensure all activities are completed in accordance with industry, utility and regulatory requirements.
Personal Attributes:
  • Strong technical and decision-making capability.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Safety-focused with a proactive mindset.
  • Commercially aware and outcomes-driven.
  • Able to lead from the front while remaining hands-on when required.
Ideal Candidate Profile:
You may currently be working as:
  • Senior Commissioning Engineer
  • Protection & Control Tester
  • Protection Engineer
  • HV Commissioning Engineer
  • Secondary Systems Engineer
  • Testing & Commissioning Engineer
  • Substation Commissioning Engineer
  • Protection & Control Engineer
  • Senior Test Engineer
  • Network Commissioning Engineer
What's On Offer:
  • Exposure to complex HV transmission, distribution and critical infrastructure projects.
  • Opportunity to work on assets up to 500kV.
  • Strong pipeline of infrastructure, utility, renewable energy and data centre projects.
  • Strong safety culture and technical excellence.
  • Long-term career development within a specialist power systems environment.
  • Opportunity to contribute to some of Australia's most significant energy and network infrastructure projects.

job.title: Shared Services Support Officer
job.description:
About the role
A Shared Services Support Officer is required for a busy, fast-paced service centre environment based in Wagga Wagga. The role is the first point of contact for customer enquiries across multiple channels and processes a range of transactions using defined processes, systems and telephony tools to support delivery of tier 0 / tier 1 services.

This full-time assignment offers 35–40 hours per week. This role is offering an ASAP start with a duration of approx 3 months. 


Duties
  • Multi-channel customer enquiries are managed and resolved at first contact where possible.
  • High-quality customer service is delivered by interpreting enquiries and providing clear, accurate responses in a shared services environment.
  • Transactions are processed accurately and efficiently using established procedures and knowledge articles to ensure consistent outcomes.
  • Complex enquiries and transactions are escalated as required, with progress updates provided to customers.
  • Multiple systems and telephony/technology solutions are used to triage work, manage tasks, enter data and maintain accurate records.
  • Team outcomes are supported through collaboration, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
  • Participation in quality assessments and operational/performance discussions is maintained, with individual KPIs met as assigned.

Skills and experience
  • Demonstrated experience in a customer-centric service environment (contact centre, service centre, shared services, corporate services, or managed services).
  • Strong communication skills and a courteous, empathic approach to customer interactions.
  • Ability to manage high volumes of varied enquiries/transactions while maintaining accuracy and service quality.
  • Confidence working across multiple computer systems, with the ability to learn new tools and processes quickly.
  • Ability to work independently to meet targets while contributing to team performance

Benefits
  • $38.89/hr + super.
  • Full-time hours in a structured shared services environment.
  • Opportunity to build experience in a high-volume, process-driven service centre.

How to apply

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.
Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced HSE Advisor for Greater Nammuldi.
Offered on a FIFO from Perth only basis, this opportunity offers the chance to work within a leading global organisation, contributing to key operational and business outcomes. Working a 5:2, 4:3 roster, you'll join a supportive team focused on safety, collaboration and delivering operational excellence.

Reporting to the HSE Superintendent, you'll use your skills and experience to support business priorities, collaborate with key stakeholders and contribute to the success of the operation. In this role, you will:

  • Utilise Enablon and Microsoft Office applications to support reporting, data collation and administrative activities
  • Coach and support leaders to improve the quality and effectiveness of safety interactions and field leadership activities

  • Mining, resources, construction or heavy industry experience highly regarded
  • Certificate IV in Work Health & Safety (WHS) and a current C Class Manual Driver's Licence
  • Strong proficiency using safety management systems, particularly Enablon, and the Microsoft Office Suite
  • Demonstrated experience coaching and supporting leaders in field-based safety activities
  • Ability to work autonomously, quickly build relationships and hit the ground running
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • Dedication to everyone's safety
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing

Why Join Chandler Macleod? Chandler Macleod is one of Australia's most experienced workforce partners. You'll receive a competitive hourly pay range paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.

Apply Now! Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading mining operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

job.title: Labourer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s leading workforce solutions providers, connecting skilled people with opportunities across some of the nation’s largest infrastructure, construction, resources and renewable energy projects.

We currently have some exciting opportunities for Labourers to join a large-scale solar farm project located in the Hunter Valley region. This is a great opportunity to gain valuable experience within the growing renewable energy sector while contributing to a significant construction project.

What's On Offer
  • Competitive hourly rates of $37-$38 per hour plus superannuation
  • Overtime opportunities
  • Monday to Friday roster
  • Opportunity to gain experience on a major renewable energy project
  • Work with an experienced construction team in a growing industry
  • Potential for ongoing project opportunities within the renewable energy sector

Key Responsibilities
As a Labourer, you will play an important role in supporting construction activities across the solar farm site. Duties may include:
  • Assisting with the installation of solar farm mechanical tracking systems
  • Mounting and installing photovoltaic (PV) solar panels
  • Operating hand and power tools safely and effectively
  • Loading, unloading, moving and distributing materials across site
  • Supporting trades and installation crews with general construction activities
  • Assisting with assembly and installation works as directed
  • Maintaining housekeeping standards and keeping work areas clean and organised
  • Performing repetitive manual handling and physically demanding tasks
  • Following site procedures, Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), and company safety requirements
About You
To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • A strong commitment to workplace health and safety
  • Reliability, punctuality and a positive work ethic
  • The ability to work effectively as part of a team
  • A willingness to undertake physically demanding work in outdoor conditions
  • Good communication skills and the ability to follow directions
  • A proactive and safety-focused approach to work
Essential Requirements
  • Valid White Card (Construction Induction Card)
  • Pre employment Mobility Assessment will be included within the recruitment process 
  • Ability to pass Drug and Alcohol Screening
  • Full Australian working rights
Highly Regarded
  • Current Driver's Licence
  • Previous labouring, construction, civil, infrastructure, or renewable energy experience
  • Experience using hand and power tools
  • Previous experience working on large-scale project sites
At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone is treated with respect and provided equal opportunity. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, genders, ages and abilities.
We are particularly committed to supporting regional employment opportunities and encourage applications from local residents of the Hunter Valley Region. 


Apply Now

Please click the Apply Now button and submit your current resume, including your contact details and residential location.

Be part of a project that's helping build a cleaner, more sustainable future for Australia.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced and commercially astute Regional Manager to take full ownership of a leading heavy vehicle and transport solutions operation, driving sales growth, workshop performance, parts operations, customer relationships, and overall branch profitability.

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on leader who understands the heavy vehicle industry from the ground up. Two opportunities are available, located in Sydney and Brisbane.

Who We're Looking For

We're seeking a genuine industry leader who has progressed from a hands-on workshop or production environment into senior management. You understand the operational realities of a heavy vehicle, manufacturing, or service-based business and combine this experience with strong commercial acumen, customer relationship management skills, and a proven ability to lead high-performing teams while driving sustainable business growth and profitability.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will have full responsibility for the strategic and operational performance of your state operation.

With complete P&L accountability, you will oversee:

• New and used equipment sales
• Workshop service, repairs and maintenance operations
• Spare parts sales and inventory management
• Customer service and after-sales support
• Safety, compliance and facility management
• Team leadership, coaching and performance

This role requires a balance of commercial acumen and operational leadership, with the ability to move seamlessly between customer meetings, sales strategy, workshop operations, and financial management.

What You'll Bring

Essential Experience
5+ years' experience leading a branch, region or business unit within:
• Heavy vehicles
• Transport equipment
• Manufacturing
• Automotive OEM
• Truck or equipment servicing operations
• Strong commercial and financial management capability
• Proven leadership experience with direct P&L responsibility
• Demonstrated success managing customer relationships and driving revenue growth
• Experience leading workshop and operational teams
Highly Desirable
• Trade qualification in Diesel Mechanics, Fabrication, Welding or a related discipline
• Experience within the heavy vehicle, transport equipment or manufacturing sectors
• Understanding of heavy vehicle repairs, maintenance and aftermarket parts operations
• Existing network across transport, logistics or fleet customers

Success in This Role Looks Like

• Achieving branch EBIT and profitability targets
• Growing equipment sales and market share
• Improving workshop productivity and turnaround times
• Expanding parts revenue and inventory performance
• Delivering exceptional customer outcomes
• Building an engaged, accountable and high-performing team

Why Join?

• Lead a significant state operation within a well-established industry leader
• Genuine autonomy with full state responsibility
• Executive-level influence and visibility
• Strong support from a national leadership team
• Opportunity to drive growth and shape the future of the business
• Competitive salary package including vehicle and incentive structure

Apply Now

If you've come from the workshop floor, understand the transport industry, and have developed into a commercially driven business leader, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your resume and cover letter via the Apply Now link.

We currently have two opportunities available, based in Sydney and Brisbane.

For a copy of the Position Description or a confidential discussion about either role, please contact Jo Ellerman on (02) 6691 9106.

job.title: Senior Development Engineer
job.description:
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Senior Development Engineer to assess and manage engineering aspects of development applications, subdivision works and major development projects. This role plays a key part in ensuring development outcomes meet engineering, environmental and community standards while protecting Council infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities
  • Assess engineering components of Development Applications (DAs), Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.
  • Supervise civil construction works associated with subdivisions and major developments.
  • Provide expert advice on stormwater, on-site detention, drainage, roads, erosion and sediment control, traffic matters and vehicle access.
  • Review engineering designs and ensure compliance with Council standards and industry best practice.
  • Prepare assessment reports, engineering conditions and recommendations within required timeframes.
  • Liaise with developers, consultants, contractors, government agencies and internal stakeholders.
  • Mentor Development Engineers and provide specialist technical advice on complex projects.
About You
You will be a highly experienced Civil Engineer with a strong background in land development, subdivision projects and development assessment.

Essential Requirements
  • Degree in Civil Engineering.
  • Current NSW Class C Driver Licence.
  • Extensive experience in development engineering, civil design and construction associated with urban development.
  • Strong knowledge of roads, drainage, stormwater, flooding, traffic and water quality management principles.
  • Experience assessing Development Applications, Subdivision Works Certificates and Subdivision Certificates.
  • Knowledge of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979 and related legislation.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
Highly Regarded
  • Local Government development engineering experience.
  • Land subdivision expertise.
  • Postgraduate qualifications in Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Working knowledge of the Local Government Act and Roads Act.
 
If you are interested in this role, please apply now or contact Andrew.murphy@Chandlermacleod.com

job.title: Project Analyst - Technology Programs
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Project Analyst - Technology Programs to support the delivery of complex transformation and project initiatives within a Federal Government environment.

About the Organisation
This Federal Government agency delivers programs and services that support Australians and their communities, working closely with stakeholders to improve outcomes through innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

About the Team
You will join a collaborative project delivery team supporting the successful delivery of complex technology and business transformation initiatives. Working alongside Project Managers, Delivery Leads, business stakeholders, and technical specialists, you will help ensure projects are effectively planned, governed, monitored, and delivered.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, analysing information, coordinating activities, and helping project teams stay on track.

About the Role
We are seeking a proactive and highly organised Project Analyst to support project delivery, reporting, governance, and coordination activities across a complex project environment.
This role will suit someone who enjoys working with data, reporting, and project information to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies. The successful candidate will be naturally curious, confident in raising concerns when required, and comfortable working across both business and technical stakeholder groups.
Rather than being a specialist scheduling role, this position focuses on project reporting, governance, program controls, stakeholder coordination, and delivery support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support the planning, coordination, and delivery of technology and business transformation projects.
  • Maintain project plans, schedules, action registers, risk and issue logs, and project documentation.
  • Monitor project milestones, deliverables, and dependencies, following up with stakeholders as required.
  • Support governance activities, including meeting papers, agendas, minutes, and project reporting.
  • Gather, analyse, and consolidate project information to support reporting and decision-making.
  • Coordinate communication and engagement across business and technical teams.
  • Identify, monitor, and escalate project risks, issues, and dependencies where required.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, presentations, briefs, and correspondence.
  • Maintain accurate project records and documentation.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, processes, and ways of working.

About You You will bring:
  • Experience supporting technology, digital, ICT, or business transformation projects within large and complex organisations.
  • Experience in PMO, Project Analyst, Project Officer, Project Coordinator, Project Controls, Scheduler, or similar roles.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience supporting project reporting, governance, and delivery activities.
  • The ability to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies and communicate them effectively to stakeholders.
  • Experience maintaining project plans, status reports, action registers, risk registers, and issue logs.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • A proactive mindset with the confidence to raise concerns and escalate issues where required.
  • Experience using Jira, Confluence, Excel, Power BI, or similar tools.

Desirable
  • Experience working within Australian Government project environments.
  • Experience working within Agile, hybrid, or multidisciplinary delivery teams.
  • Experience supporting complex programs or transformation initiatives.
  • Scheduling experience combined with broader PMO, governance, reporting, or project controls expertise.

Benefits
  • 12-month contract opportunity with Potential extension
  • $61.85 per hour + Superannuation
  • Multiple locations available across Australia: Surry Hills, NSW; Deakin, ACT; Richmond, VIC; Brisbane, QLD and Adelaide, SA

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

If this sounds like you, we encourage you to APPLY now.

job.title: Project Analyst - Technology Programs
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Project Analyst - Technology Programs to support the delivery of complex transformation and project initiatives within a Federal Government environment.

About the Organisation
This Federal Government agency delivers programs and services that support Australians and their communities, working closely with stakeholders to improve outcomes through innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

About the Team
You will join a collaborative project delivery team supporting the successful delivery of complex technology and business transformation initiatives. Working alongside Project Managers, Delivery Leads, business stakeholders, and technical specialists, you will help ensure projects are effectively planned, governed, monitored, and delivered.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, analysing information, coordinating activities, and helping project teams stay on track.

About the Role
We are seeking a proactive and highly organised Project Analyst to support project delivery, reporting, governance, and coordination activities across a complex project environment.
This role will suit someone who enjoys working with data, reporting, and project information to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies. The successful candidate will be naturally curious, confident in raising concerns when required, and comfortable working across both business and technical stakeholder groups.
Rather than being a specialist scheduling role, this position focuses on project reporting, governance, program controls, stakeholder coordination, and delivery support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support the planning, coordination, and delivery of technology and business transformation projects.
  • Maintain project plans, schedules, action registers, risk and issue logs, and project documentation.
  • Monitor project milestones, deliverables, and dependencies, following up with stakeholders as required.
  • Support governance activities, including meeting papers, agendas, minutes, and project reporting.
  • Gather, analyse, and consolidate project information to support reporting and decision-making.
  • Coordinate communication and engagement across business and technical teams.
  • Identify, monitor, and escalate project risks, issues, and dependencies where required.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, presentations, briefs, and correspondence.
  • Maintain accurate project records and documentation.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, processes, and ways of working.

About You You will bring:
  • Experience supporting technology, digital, ICT, or business transformation projects within large and complex organisations.
  • Experience in PMO, Project Analyst, Project Officer, Project Coordinator, Project Controls, Scheduler, or similar roles.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience supporting project reporting, governance, and delivery activities.
  • The ability to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies and communicate them effectively to stakeholders.
  • Experience maintaining project plans, status reports, action registers, risk registers, and issue logs.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • A proactive mindset with the confidence to raise concerns and escalate issues where required.
  • Experience using Jira, Confluence, Excel, Power BI, or similar tools.

Desirable
  • Experience working within Australian Government project environments.
  • Experience working within Agile, hybrid, or multidisciplinary delivery teams.
  • Experience supporting complex programs or transformation initiatives.
  • Scheduling experience combined with broader PMO, governance, reporting, or project controls expertise.

Benefits
  • 12-month contract opportunity with Potential extension
  • $61.85 per hour + Superannuation
  • Multiple locations available across Australia: Surry Hills, NSW; Deakin, ACT; Richmond, VIC; Brisbane, QLD and Adelaide, SA

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

If this sounds like you, we encourage you to APPLY now.
Application closes on the 28th October 2026

  At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.
You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.description:
Transfer Station Gatehouse Officer
Skye, VIC
$47 per hour + Super
Short-Term Contract until 31 January 2027
Rotating Shifts | Weekend & Public Holiday Work Required

Are you a customer-focused administrator with strong cash handling skills and experience working in waste management, logistics, transfer stations, weighbridges or similar operational environments?
We are seeking a Transfer Station Gatehouse Officer to support the day-to-day operations of a busy recycling and resource recovery facility in Skye. This is an excellent opportunity to join a collaborative team in a role that combines customer service, administration, compliance and operational support.

About the Role
Working from the gatehouse, you will be responsible for ensuring the smooth operation of site entry and exit processes, accurately processing waste disposal transactions, and providing exceptional customer service to visitors, contractors and stakeholders.
This is a shift-based position that includes weekend and public holiday work (excluding Good Friday and Christmas Day).

Key Responsibilities
  • Operate the gatehouse and weighbridge facilities
  • Assess incoming and outgoing waste types and volumes
  • Calculate and process disposal fees and charges
  • Manage cash handling, EFTPOS transactions and reconciliations
  • Maintain accurate operational records and documentation
  • Provide information and advice on waste disposal and recycling requirements
  • Monitor contractor activities and support site compliance requirements
  • Respond to customer enquiries in a professional and timely manner
  • Assist with maintaining safe, efficient and compliant site operations
About You
To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Previous experience in a waste management, transfer station, recycling facility or similar operational environment
  • Strong customer service and communication skills
  • Experience handling cash and reconciling transactions
  • Sound administration and computer skills
  • Ability to accurately assess waste types and volumes
  • Strong attention to detail and record-keeping abilities
  • The ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult customers
  • A current Victorian Driver Licence
Requirements
  • Current Victorian Driver Licence
  • Current Police Check (or willingness to obtain)
  • Availability to work rotating shifts, weekends and public holidays as required
If you're looking for a role where no two days are the same and enjoy balancing customer interaction with operational responsibility, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now with your resume

job.title: Track Protection Officer
job.description:
Track Protection Officer (TPO)

• Competitive hourly pay range + super paid on all hours worked
• 2/2 roster | FIFO from Perth
• Opportunity working at Rio Tinto at Dampier

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto's partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Track Protection Officer (TPO) to support ballast cleaning operations across the Rio Tinto Rail Network.

This is a great opportunity to join a safety-focused team working on site with Rio Tinto. You'll work alongside experienced crews, supporting day-to-day operations while contributing to safe and reliable outcomes.

Reporting to the Rail Supervisor / Superintendent, your responsibilities will include:

• Prepare, verify and implement Track Protection Plans and work-on-track authority requirements
• Confirm worksite limits, access points, safe places, adjacent line risks and protection requirements prior to starting
• Establish, maintain and remove field protection controls in accordance with approved safeworking requirements
• Conduct pre-start and safeworking briefings, including sign-on processes, hazards and emergency arrangements
• Coordinate with Train Control, supervisors, PPOs, maintainers, contractors and ballast cleaning crews to ensure safe work execution
• Monitor and respond to changing site conditions including rail traffic exposure, machine movements, fatigue, weather and scope changes
• Exercise the authority to stop work and escalate concerns immediately where protection, communication, authority or behaviours are unsafe/non-compliant
• Complete all required documentation, handovers, authority cancellations and close-out records within required timeframes

About You

• Demonstrated experience as a Track Protection Officer / Protection Officer / Safeworking professionalwithin rail maintenance or possession environments
• Experience working in heavy haul railand/or major maintenance campaigns (ballast cleaning, tamping, rail grinding, renewals or track machine operations highly regarded)
• Current Track Protection Officer competency (network relevant) and strong knowledge of safeworking systems, permits and protection authorities
• Happy to work a varied roster (12/9 and 2/2) with a mix of days and nights
• Valid Australian C-Class Driver’s Licence
• Strong teamwork and communication skills
• Dedication to everyone’s safety, including confidence to challenge unsafe work and stop the job when required
• Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing, and meet Rio Tinto onboarding, site access and VOC requirements

Why Join Chandler Macleod?

• Competitive hourly pay range paid weekly
• Superannuation paid on all hours worked
• Consistent roster and work-life balance
• Opportunity to gain experience with Rio Tinto
• Dedicated Chandler Macleod support team
• Access to future opportunities across Rio Tinto operations

Apply Now!
Ready to take the next step in your career? Join Chandler Macleod and work with Rio Tinto at one of Australia's leading mining operations. We're recruiting now and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Diversity & Inclusion
Everyone is welcome at Chandler Macleod. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and inclusive teams. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, females, neurodiverse people, people living with disability and members of the LGBTIQA+ community. Together, we're creating workplaces where people feel they belong, can be themselves and have the opportunity to thrive.

job.title: Electrical Engineer
job.description:
About the company

Our client is an established Sydney engineering company that designs, builds and services water and wastewater treatment plants for industrial clients across Australia. They’re a close-knit team where engineers see their designs go from the drawing board to a working plant.

About the role

This permanent role reports to the General Manager. You’ll own the electrical design and documentation across a variety of treatment plant projects. It’s primarily office-based, with site visits mainly at the start and completion of projects.

What you’ll do

  • Deliver electrical designs including equipment selection, circuit design and system architecture
  • Produce single line diagrams, wiring diagrams, loop diagrams and control schematics
  • Complete and document design calculations to Australian Standards
  • Specify and oversee the build of electrical control panels
  • Plan and coordinate Factory and Site Acceptance Testing (FAT/SAT)
  • Contribute to HAZOPs, design reviews and client meetings
  • Provide technical support on PLC, HMI and remote access systems
  • Keep project documentation and reporting up to date in Procore


What you’ll bring

  • A degree in Electrical Engineering
  • Experience in the water or wastewater industry: treatment plants, pump stations or utilities
  • Strong electrical design and documentation skills (AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN or similar)
  • Sound knowledge of AS/NZS 3000 and relevant Australian Standards
  • Exposure to PLC and HMI systems, control panel design and FAT/SAT
  • Organised and thorough, with strong reporting and project skills
  • Current driver’s licence


What’s on offer

  • $115,000 – $135,000 + super
  • Permanent role with real ownership of your projects
  • Direct access to the General Manager
  • Office-based in the Sutherland Shire, close to home for southern Sydney


How to apply

Click Apply with your resume. For a confidential chat, call Jayden at Chandler Macleod on 0425 481 371.

About the Role
We are seeking a proactive and highly organised Project Analyst to support project delivery, reporting, governance, and coordination activities across a complex project environment.
This role will suit someone who enjoys working with data, reporting, and project information to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies. The successful candidate will be naturally curious, confident in raising concerns when required, and comfortable working across both business and technical stakeholder groups.
Rather than being a specialist scheduling role, this position focuses on project reporting, governance, program controls, stakeholder coordination, and delivery support.

Key Responsibilities
  • Support the planning, coordination, and delivery of technology and business transformation projects.
  • Maintain project plans, schedules, action registers, risk and issue logs, and project documentation.
  • Monitor project milestones, deliverables, and dependencies, following up with stakeholders as required.
  • Support governance activities, including meeting papers, agendas, minutes, and project reporting.

  • Prepare high-quality reports, presentations, briefs, and correspondence.
  • Maintain accurate project records and documentation.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, processes, and ways of working.

About You You will bring:
  • Experience supporting technology, digital, ICT, or business transformation projects within large and complex organisations.
  • Experience in PMO, Project Analyst, Project Officer, Project Coordinator, Project Controls, Scheduler, or similar roles.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience supporting project reporting, governance, and delivery activities.
  • The ability to identify trends, risks, issues, and dependencies and communicate them effectively to stakeholders.
  • Experience maintaining project plans, status reports, action registers, risk registers, and issue logs.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • A proactive mindset with the confidence to raise concerns and escalate issues where required.
  • Experience using Jira, Confluence, Excel, Power BI, or similar tools.

Desirable

job.title: Advisor Tailings Studies
job.description:
Advisor Tailings Studies
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • 12-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
 
About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Advisor Tailings Studies.

Through its integrated operations, Rio ensures all tailings facilities meet the requirements of the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM).

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop safe tailings storage facilities for both sustaining and expansion purposes in accordance with Rio Tinto Standards and supporting the implementation of the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM) for these projects
  • Define strategic tailings capacity and decommissioning plans through interpretation of mine operational requirements and project development information.
  • Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary teams in a matrix organisation to deliver integrated tailings solutions for Concept, Order of Magnitude and Pre-feasibility Studies
  • Develop study scopes, schedules, estimates and deliverables to support progression through the project lifecycle
  • Secure alignment and endorsement of project scope, schedule, capital and other resources to support both strategic tailings capacity planning and decommissioning
  • Coordinate and engage with Operations, Responsible Dam Engineers and across broader stakeholders in both the geoscience and external approvals space to ensure the timely allocation of effort for collection of data and information to inform design, regulatory approvals and affected communities’ engagements.
  • Identify and manage project risk throughout each study phase, working closely with the Engineer of Record to integrate technical risk assessments
  • Lead the development and review of integrated facility designs with the Engineer of Record to support risk-informed decision making and demonstrate reduction of facility risk to As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP)
  • Support Feasibility Studies and Execution to ensure design intent is carried through to Operations and handover to the Responsible Dam Engineer
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Degree qualified civil engineer, geotechnical engineer, hydrogeologist, environmental engineer or metallurgist who identifies as a tailings professional. Tailings Management experience gained through consulting or operations.
  • A confident communicator with proven study leadership capability and strong safety leadership
Why Join Chandler Macleod?

Chandler Macleod is one of Australia's most experienced workforce partners. You'll receive a competitive hourly pay range paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.
